note: A dossier is every mention of a person anywhere in this archive, gathered automatically after the site is built and linked back to the page it appears on. Identity here is by NAME, not by resolved individual — where two people share a name they share this page, and the archive says so rather than guessing. Nothing on a dossier page is new evidence; it is the same evidence, brought together.

a-werdmuller-child-of-1857.r: AND BY THE AFTERNOON THERE WAS A CANDIDATE FOR THE MISSING NAME. The Queenstown Free Press of 13 February 1884 marries “CHARLES ANDREW WERDMULLER, OF STEYNSBURG, SECOND SON OF THE LATE C.J.O. WERDMULLER, OF BURGHERSDORP” to Charlotte Anne Callaghan. A man born 14 February 1857 was twenty-seven that week. NOT PROVED: no document read here names Charles Andrew’s mother, and his father — or a man of exactly that name — married again at Burgersdorp in 1874. NAMELESS IN THE INDEX, AND THAT IS THE POINT. The same sweep that found the tenth Barry child turned up a second entry with an EMPTY NAME COLUMN: born 14 February 1857, baptised 10 April 1857 at Burgersdorp, mother AUGUSTA LOUISA KOLBE, father COENRAAD JOHANNES OTTO WERDMULLER. She is the Settler's fourth daughter, born at Graaff-Reinet in 1829 — and this is the first of her children this archive has ever seen. THE CHILD'S OWN NAME IS ON THE PAGE AND NOT IN THE INDEX, so no search will ever return it. The register image has not been read; only the index line.

adriana-christina-viljoen.r: His wife, married at CRADOCK on 3 November 1828—FROM WIKITREE, NOT FROM A DOCUMENT THIS ARCHIVE HAS READ—and named with him on their daughter Anna Maria's baptism of 13 September 1835 — a daughter called after his mother, which is how this archive knows the naming ran that way in this generation too. AND SHE WAS PROBABLY HIS FIRST COUSIN. De Villiers, volume 3, under VILLION, thans VILJOEN: “(e) 12 HERCULES ALBERTUS, gedoopt 30 Maart 1777, burger te Graaff-Reinet, GEHUWD 26 FEBRUARI 1797 MET MAGDALENA BOOIJSEN”, and their seventh child is “ADRIANA CHRISTINA, GEDOOPT 19 AUGUSTUS 1810”. Magdalena Booijsen is b3c4d6, the SISTER of Petrus Jacobus — David Schalk's own father. That makes Adriana Christina eighteen in 1828 and makes him her first cousin. NOT PROVED: de Villiers records her baptism and GIVES HER NO HUSBAND, and the 1828 Cradock date is itself only on WikiTree. Right name, right age, right district, and a family already tied twice — but the weak join is the marriage record this archive has never seen.

hits.title: The documents
hits.text: Magdalena Booijsen married Hercules Albertus Viljoen in February; her brother Jan Jonathan married Hercules Albertus’s sister Judith Cornelia Theresia in May. Two households became one twice over in a single year. Thirty-one years later, David Schalk Booijzen — son of the third of those children — married Adriana Christina Viljoen at Cradock on 3 November 1828. Magdalena Booijsen’s seventh child is Adriana Christina, baptised 19 August 1810 , which makes her eighteen in 1828 and makes him her first cousin : his father and her mother were brother and sister. What is proved and what is not. De Villiers records Adriana Christina Viljoen’s baptism and gives her no husband .

Like her sister Petronella, she was sitting in this archive’s own search log two days before she had a family. THE ESTATE IS NOT READ. Youngest of the eight — and baptised at BETHULIE, the Orange Free State mission station where her father had himself been born forty-two years earlier. hits.title: The documents
hits.text: Not Ocken Johannes , as the 1891 death notice scrawled it. OCKERT JOHANNES STEPHANUS OLIVIER — all three names, exactly as her son carries them. Ockert Johannes Stephanus Booysen was called after his grandfather, entire. And she had a sister baptised at Cradock eleven months earlier: Aletta Catharina Olivier , 4 October 1823, same parents. Anna Johanna’s own daughter is Aletta Catharina Johanna . The names in this family go back up the female line and this archive could not see it until today. The namesakes → Potchefstroom, 3 July 1850 Entries 189 to 207 , June and July 1850. Three columns only: Namen der Gehuwden , Ouderdom , Wanneer gehuwd .

andries-frederick-kolbe-of-leeuwberg.r: TAKEN PRISONER IN 1901, AGED 45, AT LEEUWBERG IN THE BLOEMFONTEIN DISTRICT. TNA WO 108/368 folio 431. Sent to Cape Town and Natal. LEEUWBERG IS THE FARM COMMANDANT JOHN GERSON ELIEZAR KOLBE DIED ON, on 3 April 1868, of typhus caught on commando, leaving a widow and TWELVE CHILDREN — EIGHT SONS AND FOUR DAUGHTERS, of whom this archive can put a hand on two. THIRTY-THREE YEARS LATER A KOLBE IS STILL FARMING IT. Born about 1856, this man would have been twelve when the Commandant died, and he sits inside the age bracket of those eight sons. The farm also carries the Jephts of the 1868 horse-theft case. NO DESCENT IS DOCUMENTED AND NONE IS CLAIMED HERE — what is documented is a farm, a surname and a date. The paper that would settle it is VAB MHG M777, the 1896 estate of the Commandant’s widow ANNA JACOBA VAN DER MERWE, filed under her second husband’s name McCABE, WHICH WOULD NAME ALL TWELVE CHILDREN. Identified, unread, in Bloemfontein.
andries-frederick-kolbe-of-leeuwberg.tree: That he is one of the Commandant’s eight sons. It rests on the farm, the surname and his age, and on nothing else.

angeline-kolbe.r: A WOMAN OF THIS NAME DIES AT WAKKERSTROOM IN THE MIDDLE OF THE WAR, and this archive cannot say who she is. Twenty-eight years old, female, surname Kolbe, registered at Wakkerstroom on 15 November 1900. SHE IS NOT THE VOLKSRUST CAMP GRAVE: that is a G.E. Kolbe aged 35, a different age in a different year in a different place, and the camp was barely open in November 1900. She is not on the list of Frederik Fortunatus's eight children either — too young for Martha Angelina of 1868, too old for Catharina Maria Louisa of 1873. A daughter-in-law, most likely. THE RECORD NAMES NO PARENTS, NO HUSBAND AND NO CAUSE.

The index this archive read gives the burial as “Volksrust, Eastvaal District Council, Mpumalanga” — and that is a DISTRICT MUNICIPALITY, not a town; Wakkerstroom lies inside it.

hits.title: The documents
hits.text: The archive’s own note was careful and said “eight of their children are in the Dutch Reformed registers” — the ninth was not, and he is named for his father. The Angeline question, answered by exclusion Martha Angelina Kolbe’s record carried a warning: an Angeline Kolbe died at Wakkerstroom in 1900 , and a Martha Angeline Kolbe was buried at Volksrust in 1901 aged two months , and “neither can yet be attached to her, and this archive will not guess.” It does not have to guess now. Martha Angelina is named as an heir on her mother’s estate in 1923 and her father’s in 1929 . She was alive for both.

hits.title: The Kolbes
hits.text: Their father outlived them both by thirty-six years. Daniel's death registration carries the words G A Kolbe's son , which the index mangled into G A Kolbelsson — and that misprint is the line that ties the graves to the old man. Two women the war took, and one this archive cannot name Angeline Kolbe , aged 28, died at Wakkerstroom on 15 November 1900 . Martha Angeline Kolbe , born 9 October 1901, died 8 December 1901, buried at Volksrust — sixty days old. Volksrust held a concentration camp, and this archive records the burial place without claiming the cause, because it has read no camp register that names the child. Angeline is not the camp grave NAAIRS holds — that is a G.E.

hits.text: The death registration is right within a year; THE 1879 MARRIAGE ENTRY IS WRONG BY SIX YEARS. He was 28 when he married, not 22. → Jacobus Nicolaas Booysen / Booyzen Two brothers, born 1840 and 1841, both dying on 17 November 1882. Serious Almost certainly one man entered twice under the two spellings of the surname. → Anna Catharina Booysen 1842–1960. Reject One hundred and eighteen years old. A typing error, probably for 1860 or 1906. George Augustus Kolbe (1802–1844) Julia Kolbe born 1846, two years after his death; seven consistency issues in all. Resolved RESOLVED. His 1845 death notice (estate 7698) and his gravestone both give 1 December 1844, and neither his notice nor his widow’s 1867 notice lists a Julia.

hits.title: What changed
hits.text: Still marked Serious. This archive is not going to decide a father on a city. THE OTHER MOVED FURTHER THAN EXPECTED. Ockert Johannes Stephanus Olivier and Anna Catharina Botha MARRIED AT GRAAFF-REINET ON 8 DECEMBER 1816 — index only, no image — and have four children baptised at Cradock between 1820 and 1826: Gert Cornelis, Aletta Catharina, Anna Johanna and an Ockert Johannes Stephanus the younger. GRAAFF-REINET is the Booysens' own town.

hits.title: The documents
hits.text: Cradock, 4 October 1824 The Cradock doopregister for 1824 — the church her family baptised in, and the district her death notice gives sixty-seven years later. Child Anna Johanna Olivier , born 10 September 1824 Baptised 4 October 1824 , Cradock Father Ockert Johannes Stephanus Olivier Mother Anna Catharina Botha Read her father’s name again. Not Ocken Johannes , as the 1891 death notice scrawled it. OCKERT JOHANNES STEPHANUS OLIVIER — all three names, exactly as her son carries them. Ockert Johannes Stephanus Booysen was called after his grandfather, entire. And she had a sister baptised at Cradock eleven months earlier: Aletta Catharina Olivier , 4 October 1823, same parents.

hits.title: The Name
hits.text: De Villiers, volume 3, entry 876: “ Willem Slier, van Hamburg , gehuwd 19 November 1780 met Anna Catharina Fortman.” It is a German name. Schlier or Schleer, spoken by a Hamburger and written down by Cape clerks who had never seen it on paper — which is exactly how one woman ends up with five surnames in five documents inside one lifetime. Nobody argues that the Sliers changed their name. Nobody proposes that Hier is a branch of the family or that Schleher marks a generation.

anna-catharina-johanna-olivier.v: Anna Johanna Booijzen, gebooren Oliefier (1891) · Anna Catrena (1891) · born Olivier (1908)
anna-catharina-johanna-olivier.r: THE FIRST WIFE OF HENDRIK STEFANUS BOOIJSEN, and for a week this archive had her filed as a stranger. Her own Sterfkennis 6332 gives her parents as OCKEN JOHANNES OLIEFIER and ANNA JOHANNA BOTHA, her age as 67 years 8 months and 1 day, her farm as BRAKFONTEIN — which this archive read as Boekfontein — and her surname as OLIEFIER, which this archive read as Alberts. She was still married when she died: her husband outlived her by seventeen years and remarried at Zeerust eleven months later. Seven children, all of age: Petrus Jacobus, Ocken Johannes, Anna Johanna Maria, Elesabettha Maria Cornelya, Alettha Catrina Johanna, Magdalena Johanna, Hendrick Stefanus Nicolaas. Her father is where OCKERT JOHANNES came into this family — and her 1824 baptism gives his name entire, OCKERT JOHANNES STEPHANUS OLIVIER, which is exactly what her son was called. She married Hendrik Stephanus Booijzen at POTCHEFSTROOM on 3 JULY 1850, entry 206, she 25 and he 23 — the earliest evidence this archive has of this family north of the Vaal, twenty-six years before the 1876 death at Rustenburg and two years before the Sand River Convention.

What was withdrawn → Since then the second of those two has been settled. The farm is Brakfontein , not Boekfontein, and the maiden name is Oliefier , not Alberts. She is Anna Catharina Johanna Olivier , the first wife of Hendrik Stefanus Booijsen, and she died on the family's own farm. How that was read → 1937–38 · A whole estate, from the death to the last shilling Estates 58379 and 58380 , KAB MOOC 6/9/5047 — on this archive's Sources page as "Located, not yet read" for months. Put together, she is Anna Catharina Johanna Olivier , and every one of them agrees on the surname. Seven children, all of age Question twelve, entire. "Allen mondig." anna-catharina-sleer.v: Slier · Schleher · Sher · Hier — five renderings, five sources
anna-catharina-sleer.r: Lived to ninety-eight. Married James Montjoy 9 Mar 1817 at Graaff-Reinet, having first been the widow of a Pietersen. 15 SEPTEMBER 2026 — SHE HAS PARENTS, A BAPTISM AND THREE SIBLINGS. De Villiers's volume 3, entry 876: “WILLEM SLIER, VAN HAMBURG, gehuwd 19 November 1780 met ANNA CATHARINA FORTMAN — (b) 1 ANNA CATHARINA, GEDOOPT 14 OCTOBER 1787, GEHUWD MET HERMANUS PIETERSE; 2 Wilhelmina Christina, gedoopt 27 December 1789, gehuwd 5 Januari 1811 met Jan Abraham van Wijk, van Amsterdam; 3 Geertruida Johanna, gedoopt 2 Juli 1791; 4 Wilhelmus Josephus, gedoopt 5 Maart 1797.” AND THE FIVE SPELLINGS STOP BEING A MYSTERY: a Hamburg name — Schlier, Schleer — written down by Cape clerks who had never seen it. She married Hermanus Pietersen on 5 APRIL 1807 at nineteen, was a widow by March 1817, a widow again by September 1827, and lived until 1885. FIFTY-EIGHT YEARS A WIDOW.

hits.title: What was taken back
hits.text: The FamilySearch collection is titled “Johannesburg Cemetery Records” and the index repeats that label for every register inside it, including those of other municipalities. The collection title is not the place. how A document read wrongly, or a conclusion drawn past what the document says. Where it lives now → 13 Sep 2026 was “Anna J. Mary Booyzen and George Downing Daschner were stillborn or died the same day” now Both lived. She was SIX MONTHS old and he was THREE MONTHS AND FIVE DAYS. The Brixton register keeps Years, Months and Days in three separate columns and FamilySearch's index collapses them into one field, so a child with the Years column blank comes out as “0 days”.

hits.title: The documents
hits.text: Born Cape Province. Indwe. Married. Since 1908. Forty-seven in July 1932 against twenty-two in September 1908 — which makes him forty-six. One year. Brixton Cemetery, 31 July 1932 , where the burial register gives his birth as 1885 and where this family already buries its Johannesburg dead: Anna J. Mary Booyzen in 1914, John Barry Booyzen in 1916, George Downing Daschner in 1925. And “Sasanna Adriana Booyzen” was buried at Johannesburg in 1968 — his widow, under his name, thirty-six years after him. What does not No parents are named , because a South African civil death registration does not ask for them unless the deceased is under ten.

anna-jacoba-van-der-merwe.r: SHE REMARRIED, AND HER SECOND HUSBAND IS WHY SHE WAS HARD TO FIND. The Free State archives hold her under a different surname: VAB MHG M777 — “MCCABE, ANNA JACOBA. NOOIENSVAN VAN DER MERWE. EGGENOTE JOHN GHERSON [KOLBE]”, 1896. WIDOWED IN 1868 WITH TWELVE CHILDREN AND DEAD TWENTY-EIGHT YEARS LATER AS MRS MCCABE. Her husband’s own estate is beside it — VAB MHG K71, “KOLBE, JOHN GERSON ELEAZAR. EGGENOTE ANNA JACOBA (GEBORE VAN DER MERWE)”, 1868. AND THE McCABE NAME IS ALREADY IN THIS ARCHIVE: a ROSA MAGDALENA KOLBE was baptised at Bloemfontein in 1890 to Frederik Fortuna Kolbe and MARIA PETRONELLA ELIZABETH ANTOINETTA MCCABE — a second Kolbe–McCabe marriage in the same small Free State world, and this archive does not yet know whether that is a coincidence. 20 SEPTEMBER 2026 — IT MAY NOT BE ONE. On a Geni profile, the FREDERIK FORTUNATA KOLBE of that baptism is the COMMANDANT’S OWN SON, born 1857 at Bloemfontein — so the Commandant’s widow married FRANCIS McCABE the Landdrost about April 1871, and her son married a McCABE. McCabe died ten months later leaving “four sons and two daughters, BESIDES A LARGE FAMILY OF STEP-CHILDREN”. THE TWO HOUSEHOLDS WERE ONE FOR ELEVEN MONTHS, and a marriage across them afterwards is ordinary rather than remarkable. AND THIS ARCHIVE ALREADY HELD THE OTHER HALF WITHOUT NOTICING. VAB MHG C129, the 1872 estate index for FRANCIS McCABE, names his FIRST wife as MARIA PETRONELLA ELISABETHA ANTOINETTA RAATH — and the Bloemfontein baptism of 1890 names the mother as MARIA PETRONELLA ELIZABETH ANTOINETTA McCABE. THE SAME FOUR-PART NAME, CARRYING McCABE AS A SURNAME: she is almost certainly his daughter by Raath, named for her mother entire. So a stepbrother married a stepsister, nine years after their parents’ eleven-month marriage, and McCabe’s obituary had already said he left “four sons and two daughters, BESIDES A LARGE FAMILY OF STEP-CHILDREN”. THE ONE LINK THAT IS FROM A USER TREE AND NOT FROM A DOCUMENT is that her husband is the Commandant’s son; it is not adopted, and VAB MHG C129 would settle it by naming the daughters. NEITHER ESTATE IS READ. M777 is the document that would name the twelve children. Married JOHN GERSON ELIEZAR KOLBE on 3 APRIL 1843 and was widowed on the same date twenty-five years later. She is the third van der Merwe to marry into these families. 15 SEPTEMBER 2026 — McCABE HAS A FIRST NAME, A BIRTH DATE AND AN OFFICE. He is FRANCIS McCABE, LANDDROST OF BLOEMFONTEIN, son of Dr Patrick McCabe, a Staff-Assistant Surgeon attached to the British Army on the Cape Frontier, born at one of the military posts in what is now British Kaffraria on 29 SEPTEMBER 1817. His obituary in The Friend says he “married his second wife about ten months since — THE WIDOW OF THE LATE COMMANDANT J.G.E. KOLBE, OF KAFIRBERG, NEAR THIS TOWN”, and he died suddenly of heart disease on the Modder River road on 23 FEBRUARY 1872, aged 54, leaving “a widow, four sons and two daughters, BESIDES A LARGE FAMILY OF STEP-CHILDREN”. SO: MARRIED 3 APRIL 1843, WIDOWED 3 APRIL 1868 WITH TWELVE CHILDREN, MARRIED AGAIN ABOUT APRIL 1871, WIDOWED AGAIN FIFTEEN MONTHS LATER, AND DEAD IN 1896 UNDER HIS NAME. For about eleven months there were eighteen children attached to one household. She was living at SPRINGFIELD, WARD UPPER MODDER-RIVER, DISTRICT BLOEMFONTEIN in October 1868, when a black mare and foal of hers were stolen — the court record that says so is the only document this archive has that shows her doing anything at all.

hits.title: What changed
hits.text: DOROTHEA REGINA AND RUBEN JACOBUS JOSUAH ARE NOT ON IT, and this archive had both as children “named on the 1915 death notice”. They are grandchildren: a Dorothea Regina baptised at Slang River in 1892 and a Ruben Jacobus Hosea at Dordrecht in 1888, both to Henry Nicholas Barry and Anna Johanna Maria Schoeman. The page also gives Margaretha Kolbe's death as 2 AUGUST 1912, where this archive had only the year. And it says the marriage took place at “Burghersdorp (probably)” — a son of the house, writing in English with a solicitor's help, who did not know where his parents married and put it in brackets.

hits.title: The documents
hits.text: The tree is wrong three times over. Boomkweker Not a miner, and not yet a railwayman. In 1924 George grew trees. A wholly new occupation for him — and by 1947 he was a clerk on the South African Railways . Both were living at Evaton — where Anna's grandmother Anna Johanna Maria Schoeman had died the year before. The whole connection had moved north together. 1947 · The death registration, and a garbled memory vindicated Entry 10,899 , Johannesburg, registered 12 December 1947 — a second document, distinct from the death notice.

anna-maria-van-der-merwe.r: WikiTree makes her a daughter of DAVID SCHALK VAN DER MERWE and ANNA ELIZABETH LOUW—which, if right, is where the forename DAVID SCHALK entered this family: her eldest son carries her father’s names entire.FROM WIKITREE, NOT FROM A DOCUMENT THIS ARCHIVE HAS READ, and it is checkable against the van der Merwe baptism registers rather than the tree. 15 SEPTEMBER 2026 — DE VILLIERS HAS HER, AND HE DISAGREES WITH THE TREE. Volume 2 of the Geslacht-register der oude Kaapsche familien, in the van der Merwe genealogy: “(e) 3 WILLEM, gedoopt 30 September 1764, burger te Stellenbosch, gehuwd 7 November 1784 met HESTER MARIA VAN DER MERWE — (f) 1 Johanna Catharina, gedoopt 8 Maart 1787; 2 ANNA MARIA, GEDOOPT 5 OCTOBER 1788, GEHUWD MET PETRUS JACOBUS BOOIJSEN; 3 DAVID SCHALK, GEDOOPT 10 OCTOBER 1790; 4 Hendrina Magdalena, 1792; 5 Hester Maria, 1793; 6 Hendrik Petrus Jacobus, 1796.” SO THE TREE MAKES DAVID SCHALK HER FATHER AND THE BOOK MAKES HIM HER BROTHER, and the two parentages cannot both be right. BUT THE CONCLUSION SURVIVES EITHER READING: on both accounts the name stands one step from her. A BAPTISM DATE AT LAST, AND IT IS FOURTEEN DAYS AFTER HIS — he on 21 September 1788, she on 5 October. His wife, married 1805 at Graaff-Reinet — and DOCUMENTED, which she was not until today. A Dutch Reformed baptism of 4 JANUARY 1807 names her as the mother of DAVID SCHALK BOOIJZEN, born 12 December 1806, who is FIRST of the eight children on the 1876 Sterfkennis. That resolves a contradiction this archive marked Serious (they were married by 1806, so the 1825 Cape Town marriage record is a different couple) and it rewrites the wall on the ancestor chart, which said only a family tree put her there. WHAT IS STILL NOT PROVED is that she is the mother of the 1812 man in the direct line.

hits.text: Page 78 then gives her husband as JAN BOOIJSEN, baptised 29 January 1741, and their SEVENTH CHILD as “Petrus Jacobus, gedoopt 21 September 1788, gehuwd met Anna Maria van der Merwe”, whose first child is “David Schalk, gedoopt 4 Januari 1807”. FOUR FIELDS AGREE WITH THIS ARCHIVE AND THE FIFTH IS THE FATHER. anna-maria-viljoen.v: the mother of the Burgersdorp Kolbes
anna-maria-viljoen.r: A WOMAN THIS ARCHIVE DID NOT HOLD UNTIL THE LAST 214 IMAGES OF THE BURGERSDORP REGISTER WERE READ. She is named as the mother at three fonts in one book: GEORGE AUGUSTUS, born 2 October 1861, baptised 12 January 1862; ANNA JOHANNA, born 29 December 1863, baptised 28 February 1864; PETRUS JACOBUS, born 11 August 1865, baptised 8 October 1865. Her husband is entered as “G A Kolbe” at the first and “George Augustus Kolbe” at the other two. HER ELDEST SON IS THE MAN ON THE WAKKERSTROOM STONE AND THE PRISONER OF WO 108/368. Nothing else of her is known — no marriage, no parents, no death. VILJOEN IS A NAME THIS ARCHIVE ALREADY CARRIES, through Adriana Christina Viljoen, and no connection is claimed.

hits.title: The documents
hits.text: Utrecht and Vryheid sit either side of Wakkerstroom on the Natal–Transvaal border. This is not three children who happened to marry in one town. It is a household that moved from the Orange River to the Natal border and stayed. And one that reaches across to the other branch. The same index holds “Anna Maria Viljoen Kolbe” with a Natal estate ( 1:1:QPHZ-23XS ) — the woman found this morning in the Burgersdorp baptism register as the mother of the other George Augustus Kolbe, the one born in 1861 and buried at Wakkerstroom. Both Kolbe households ended up in the same corner of Natal. Sixty-four Kolbe entries in that collection and this archive has read none of the files.

anna-van-der-merwe-of-burgersdorp.r: The third godparent at the 1853 Barry font, and the only one who is not a Kolbe. A VAN DER MERWE standing at a Barry christening at Burgersdorp — a surname this archive has been chasing on the entirely other side of the family, among the Booysens of Graaff-Reinet. Not connected, and set down so the coincidence is on the record.

augusta-louisa-kolbe.r: THE SETTLER'S FOURTH DAUGHTER HAS THREE DOCUMENTS AND THIS ARCHIVE HAD NONE OF THEM. A WILL, MADE IN 1868 AND FILED IN 1873: KAB MOOC 7/1/332 no. 205, “KOLBE, AUGUSTA LOUISA. WIFE OF COENRAAD JOHANNES OTTO WERDMULLER VAN ELGG” — which is the first document read here that ties her to that man by anything but a newspaper. A DEATH NOTICE, MOOC 6/9/145 no. 9981, 1873. And a LIQUIDATION AND DISTRIBUTION ACCOUNT, MOOC 13/1/299 no. 93, 1874, which means there was something to distribute. SHE DIED IN 1873 AND HER HUSBAND REMARRIED IN JULY 1874 — a year and a month, which is what a widower does, and which settles the question this archive left open yesterday about whose son Charles Andrew is. NONE OF THE THREE IS READ.

baba-booyzen.r: A TWELFTH CHILD, AND THE ONLY WORD CUT FOR HER OR HIM IS “BABA”. The centre pillar of the Silverton stone lists twelve children by their household names; the 1940 estate lists eleven by their registered ones; and when the two are set side by side EVERY ONE OF THE ELEVEN IS CLAIMED EXACTLY ONCE, leaving “✝ BABA” — a birth star, a cross, and no name — with nothing to match. Not on the estate because the child was already dead when it was written. NO DATE, NO SEX, NO NAME, NO ORDER beyond the stone's own. This archive has met the shape before: Joseph Heinrich Daschner's 1942 notice named eleven children and the Brixton register produced a twelfth. A death notice lists the living; a gravestone, cut by the family, lists the children.

hits.text: The register → A death notice lists the living. A gravestone, cut by the family, lists the children. That is the difference between the two documents, and it is worth more than either of them alone. What is not claimed. No birth date, no sex, no order of birth beyond the stone's own order, and no name — the child is entered here as Baba Booyzen because that is the only word cut for it. The matches above are readings of nicknames, not documents, and the household page marks every one of them as inferred rather than stated. The mother's own name is on the stone as Betie 's: the family reused it inside one generation. What was searched today and not found Four questions worked properly and answered no , or not yet .

beatrix-magdalena-catharina-boshoff.r: HER HALF OF THE SILVERTON STONE READS: “AAN ONS DIERBARE MOEDER — BEATRIX MAGDALENA CATHARINA (GEB. BOSHOFF) — ✳ 18-7-1888, † 23-5-1977 — Deur Jesus was vrede behaal, sy kruisdood het alles betaal. Ges. 12:6”. THE DEATH IS NEW AND THE BIRTH DISAGREES WITH THIS ARCHIVE. Her baptism at Mossel Bay on 16 February 1890 gives her born 16 JUNE 1889; the stone says 18 JULY 1888, and the eGGSA index transcribes it 1889. A baptism register written weeks after the event outranks a stone cut eighty-eight years later, so this archive keeps 1889 — and records the disagreement rather than hiding it. BURIED AT SILVERTON, PRETORIA, on a joint stone with her husband: “nee BOSHOFF 1889-1977”. The birth year matches her 1890 Mossel Bay baptism and 1977 is a death year this archive did not have. IMAGE LOCATED, NOT YET READ. His widow, who signed the 1940 death notice at Pretoria on 26 July 1940 — and who could not name her husband's parents. SHE WAS SIXTEEN when she married him at Mosselbaai on 5 September 1905, with her parents consenting; he was thirty. Her own parents were EVERT PHILIP BOSHOFF and SUSANNA FREDERIKA ALETTA MEYER, named on her 1890 baptism — and two of her eleven children are called straight after them.

It is the difference between a record and a corroborated record , and it took one search and five photographs. 1940 · The pillar at Silverton — twelve household names, matched to eleven legal ones The centre pillar of the double stone at Silverton lists the children of Stefanus Francois Booyzen and Beatrix Magdalena Catharina Boshoff by the names they were called at home. His 1940 estate lists eleven children by the names they were registered under. The two lists have never been set side by side, and doing it identifies a twelfth child. hits.text: What has changed is that the one false positive has been opened and turns out to be his mother-in-law. So the van Niekerks are now documented. catharina-johanna-helena-beyleveldt.v: Byleveld · “Booyzen Byleveld Langenbog Booyzen”, in the Cape civil register
catharina-johanna-helena-beyleveldt.r: AND HER ESTATE IS FINDABLE: “MOOC 6/9/4898 · 54123 — BOOYZEN, CATHARINA JOHANNA HELENA, NEE BEYLEVELD. ESTATE PAPERS. 1937”, Cape Town Archives Repository. A file that would name her parents, her husband and her children, and would settle in one page whether she belongs to this family. NOT READ. NOT THIS FAMILY so far as anything here can show, AND RECORDED BECAUSE SHE IS THE FOURTH BOOYZEN STONE IN THAT CEMETERY. “HIER RUS — CATHARINA JOHANNA HELENA BOOYZEN (GEB. BEYLEVELDT) — GEB. 7 JANUARIE 1855 — OORL. 16 MAART 1937.” The Cape Province civil register carries her under a chain of surnames that is its own biography — BOOYZEN BYLEVELD LANGENBOG BOOYZEN — and gives her born 1857 where the stone says 1855. Her Cape probate names her husband as JOHANNES HENDRIK. She died on 16 MARCH 1937, TWELVE WEEKS BEFORE PIETER J. BOOYZEN went into the same ground, and this archive can find no link between them but the surname and the town. SET DOWN SO THAT NOBODY LATER ASSUMES ONE.

hits.title: What changed
hits.text: MIJNWERKER — an eighth child, and the last line of the testimony Found found Four documents from the Dutch Reformed congregation at Indwe, found by typing “Indwe” into the register that was built yesterday. A Willem Hermanus BOOIJZEN, aged 21, is confirmed there on 31 May 1907, in a class that also holds Catharina Maria Elizabeth Roodt, 17, and Susanna Adriana Roodt, 15. On 21 September 1908 he marries Susanna Adriana Roodt, sixteen, at Indwe — certificate 13, her parents consenting — and under Rang of Beroep the register writes MIJNWERKER, of DUGMORE MIJN.

catharina-maria-sophia-booysen.d: 1946 — West Park, grave 51, beside her husband
catharina-maria-sophia-booysen.r: Baptised at Barkly Oost 24 May 1891, entry 120, named for her mother entire, and fourteen when her father died at Indwe. She married Joseph Heinrich Daschner AT INDWE — the same village — and his 1942 death notice names her “born Booyzen”, with a z, in a Johannesburg typist’s hands. Eleven children, five of them carrying Booyzen and Barry forenames. She died in the Transvaal in 1946 — estate TAB MHG 3734/46, found only when this archive finally searched outside the Cape, and still to be read.

The children of Catharina Maria Sophia Booysen — Kathleen Barry's daughter — on her husband's 1942 death notice. Kathleen Barry married a Booyzen in the 1880s, so the surname stops with her. Her daughter married a Daschner, so it is two surnames gone in two generations.

catharine-sophia-maria-kolbe.v: Catharine Kolbe (1853) · Catharine Sophia Maria Kolber (1848)
catharine-sophia-maria-kolbe.r: SHE IS WHERE THE NAME COMES FROM, and this archive had her down as “Catharine Kolbe” and nothing more. On 13 November 1848 she stood godmother at Graaff-Reinet to her sister Margaretha's son HENRY JAMES BARRY, entry 603, and the clerk wrote her out in full: CATHARINE SOPHIA MARIA KOLBER. ELEVEN YEARS LATER her sister named a daughter CATHERINE MARIA SOPHIA — the Kathleen Barry who married into this family — and the name then ran through four more generations and three more surnames. This archive had called it a Barry name. It is a Kolbe name, and it belongs to a woman who never married into the Booyzens at all. She is also godmother at Burgersdorp in 1853, two entries above her sister Mary Elizabeth's son.

hits.title: What changed
hits.text: Two fonts, a year apart, and every witness a Kolbe Found found Having read one Barry baptism, the one before it was worth reading too. At the 1847 font the witnesses are John Kolbe, Margaret Kolbe and Augusta Kolbe; at the 1848 font, Catharine Sophia Maria Kolbe. Two children, two years, and not a Barry witness between them. That is the same conclusion the namesake correction reached from one entry, arrived at a second time from another — the names this archive has called Barry names belong to the people who stood at the fonts, and they were all Kolbes.

catherine-mary-sophia-barry-of-1855.r: THE TENTH CHILD, FOUND BY READING 267 REGISTER IMAGES — and she has the same name as her sister. Burgersdorp doopregister, image group 008039088, image 427: born 10 JULY 1855, baptised 22 JULY 1855, father JOHN BARRY, mother MARGARET LOUISA KOLBE. FOUR YEARS LATER THE SAME PARENTS BAPTISED ANOTHER CATHARINA MARY SOPHIA at Dordrecht, born 4 August 1859 — the woman who married into the Booyzens and carried the name to Australia. TWO DAUGHTERS, ONE NAME, DIFFERENT BIRTHDAYS FOUR YEARS APART IN DIFFERENT TOWNS. A baptism is not done twice, so the ordinary reading is the ordinary Cape practice: THIS CHILD DIED, AND THE NAME WAS GIVEN AGAIN. This archive has no burial for her and states the death only as “before August 1859”. AND SHE EXPLAINS THE NAME TWICE OVER: the archive has already shown CATHERINE MARIA SOPHIA is a Kolbe name, off the 1848 godmother Catharine Sophia Maria Kolber. hits.title: The Booyzen Archive
hits.text: There is no photograph of their farm, and this archive does not invent one. This archive was built for David Defranceski , born in Johannesburg, living in Brisbane. It runs backwards from his grandmother Catherine Mary Sophia Booyzen (1929–2013) — who married Nuno Fernando Lerena at St Joseph's, Mayfair, in 1949 — into the north-eastern Cape: to Barkly East and Dordrecht , to Cradock and Graaff-Reinet , and out again to Württemberg , to Soho , and to a County Cork that may or may not be real. It is a public archive with one rule: the living are left out — omitted, not hidden.

hits.title: The Barrys
hits.text: The 1915 death notice shows she is the same woman as Kathleen above. Withdrawn. Read rows five and seven together. Catherina Maria Sophia Barry died on 30 July 1859. Catherine Maria Sophia Barry was born on 4 August 1859 — five days later , and was given the dead child's name. That name then travelled: to Catherine Mary Sophia Booyzen (1891–1946) , and to Catherine Mary Sophia Booyzen (1929–2013) , David Defranceski's grandmother. A four-year-old's death in Burgersdorp is still being commemorated, unknowingly, four generations later.

hits.title: The cousin marriage
hits.text: George was Kathleen's son. Anna was Hendrik's granddaughter. They were first cousins once removed , and their common ancestors are John Augustus Barry I and Margaretha Wilhelmina Elizabeth Mary Kolbe . What follows from it Catherine Mary Sophia Booyzen descends from John Augustus Barry I and Margaretha Kolbe twice — once through her father, once through her mother. This is pedigree collapse : she has fewer distinct ancestors than the arithmetic of generations predicts. Where a person five generations back should have thirty-two separate ancestors, she has thirty — because one couple occupies two of the slots.

hits.title: Method
hits.text: Disputed Asserted somewhere in the record and contradicted somewhere else in it. Every one is listed. Disputed → The living are left out Living people are omitted from this build entirely — not hidden, not gated, not present in the output. Because this line reaches the present within three generations of Catherine Mary Sophia Booyzen, that removes a large part of the story from public view. Cheryl Anne Lerena , David Defranceski's mother, appears only as a name and a birth year where the descent cannot be explained without her. Her siblings' living descendants do not appear at all. A removal request is honoured within days, without argument and without requiring a reason. Where this one starts Unusually well.

charles-andrew-werdmuller.r: THE DATES NOW CLOSE AROUND HIM, THOUGH NO DOCUMENT YET NAMES HIS MOTHER. His father’s first wife, AUGUSTA LOUISA KOLBE, MADE A WILL IN 1868 AND DIED IN 1873 — KAB MOOC 7/1/332 no. 205, “KOLBE, AUGUSTA LOUISA, WIFE OF COENRAAD JOHANNES OTTO WERDMULLER VAN ELGG”, filed 1873 — and his father remarried on 7 JULY 1874. IN 1882 CHARLES ANDREW WAS IN BUSINESS WITH HIS FATHER as C.A. Werdmuller and Company, and in February 1884 he married. A SON OF THE 1874 MARRIAGE WOULD HAVE BEEN SEVEN AND NINE. He can only be a child of the first marriage, and the first wife is the Settler’s daughter. THE ONE LOOPHOLE LEFT is an earlier wife before Augusta Louisa, and his father’s 1882 DEATH NOTICE would close it by naming the children. SECOND SON OF THE LATE C.J.O. WERDMULLER OF BURGHERSDORP, married at Wesley Church, Queenstown, on 13 FEBRUARY 1884 to CHARLOTTE ANNE CALLAGHAN, eldest daughter of Hugh Callaghan of Ashby Manor. Of STEYNSBURG then, and by 1909 CHARLES WERDMULLER, J.P., OF HOOPSTAD in the Orange River Colony — the town his wife died in. HIS MOTHER IS NOT NAMED ON ANYTHING READ HERE. If he is the child born 14 February 1857 at Burgersdorp he is AUGUSTA LOUISA KOLBE’S SON and a grandson of the 1820 Settler; if he belongs to his father’s 1874 marriage he is no relation at all, and a man marrying in 1884 as a second son cannot be. THE DATES FAVOUR KOLBE AND THE DOCUMENTS DO NOT SAY IT.

charles-kolbe.v: the first of two sons given that name
charles-kolbe.r: ONE OF THE EIGHT SONS, NAMED FOR THE FIRST TIME. Father John, mother Mary. Batch C15051-2. HIS DEATH IS NOT IN THE GERMAN LUTHERAN REGISTER, which holds six other Kolbe burials — but a second son was christened CHARLES Samuel nine years later, and families reused a name when the first child carrying it had died. That is an inference and not a record.
charles-kolbe.tree: That he died before 1807. It rests on the reuse of the name, not on a burial entry.

charles-petrus-barend-lowies.r: Her first husband, and estate 7081 — the OTHER number cited in the Remarks column of the 1905 marriage register. Born in the district of CRADOCK about 1849, within a year of David Schalk Booysen and in the same Karoo district; dead at Pretoria, where David Schalk had been widowed five years earlier. His parents were JAN LOWIES and ELISABETHA MARIA LUBBE, and he left TWELVE children. THE FILE IS NOW READ. He was a HAWKER, of GOEDEHOOP, PRETORIA — which is the exact address David Schalk Booyzen gave on the marriage register three weeks later, so the two men lived in the same place. Dutch, of the Cradock district, 56 years and 8 months, dead in the LUNATIC ASYLUM at Pretoria on 5 June 1905. Movables but no land, an estate over £100, and a will. Six of the twelve children were still minors. His widow signed the notice on 27 October and married David Schalk on 27 November.

hits.title: What changed
hits.text: 7081 is the bride's, and it is CHARLES PETRUS BAREND LOWIES — born in the DISTRICT OF CRADOCK about 1849, dead at PRETORIA on 5 JUNE 1905, parents Jan Lowies and Elisabetha Maria Lubbe, TWELVE children. Read the two men together: David Schalk Booijzen born Cradock 9 June 1848 and widowed at Pretoria in 1900; Charles Petrus Barend Lowies born district Cradock about 1849 and dead at Pretoria in 1905. Two men born a year apart in one Karoo district, both ending in Pretoria — and five months and twenty-two days after the second died, the first married his widow. The Master cleared both estates within four days: 4795 on 4 November, 7081 on the 7th, the wedding on the 27th.

hits.title: The documents
hits.text: 4795 was David Schalk’s and led back to his first wife’s death notice. This is 7081 , read entire — and it is not the document this archive expected. Death Notice 7081 , filed 28 October 1905 . Under The Administration of Estates Proclamation, 1902 — the same wartime proclamation as the Marais notice. The form, as completed 1. Name Charles Petrus Barend Lowies , of GOEDEHOOP, PRETORIA 2. Birthplace Dutch, CRADOCK DISTRICT, Cape Colony 3. Father Jan Lowies 3. Mother Elizabetha Maria Lowies, born LUBBE 4. Age 56 years 8 months — born about October 1848 5. Occupation HAWKER 6a. Spouse Johanna Elena Lowies, born Stols , in community of property 6b. Previous spouses “No pre-deceased spouse or spouses” 6c. Married at Pretoria 7. Died 5 June 1905 8.

charlotta-elizabetha-dormehl.r: His second wife, married at Zeerust on 14 April 1892 when she was fifty-one and he sixty-three, and her own Death Notice 844 gives the rest: born Graaff-Reinet about October 1841, FARMER'S WIFE, father JACOB DORMEHL and mother UNKNOWN, dead at Driefontein in Groot Marico on 6 February 1902 aged 60 years 4 months, leaving ONE WAGON AND HOUSEHOLD FURNITURE worth £51 8s 0d and a will. THREE HUSBANDS — Jacob van Staden, then Matthys Roos, then Booysen — and SIX CHILDREN, two van Stadens and four Rooses, NOT ONE OF THEM A BOOYSEN. That is why the four children this archive once drew under her are not hers.

charlotte-anne-callaghan.d: 17 Feb 1891, Hoopstad, Orange Free State — aged 32
charlotte-anne-callaghan.r: ELDEST DAUGHTER OF HUGH CALLAGHAN, ESQ., OF ASHBY MANOR, district of Queenstown; married Charles Andrew Werdmuller on 13 February 1884. SEVEN YEARS LATER SHE WAS DEAD AT THIRTY-TWO, at Hoopstad, “after a long illness”, and a correspondent’s obituary in the Queenstown Free Press adds that she had arrived there only a few months before, in indifferent health, with a disorder of the heart that proved organic. SHE LEFT “A HUSBAND AND TWO LITTLE GIRLS”, and it is that line which lets the 1909 marriage notice call Amy a second daughter.

charlotte-kolbe.r: Aged 30 in the Conduit Street household at the 1841 census. FROM THE CENSUS. 17 SEPTEMBER 2026 — SHE IS NOT IN THE 1851 CENSUS AND SHE PROBABLY DID NOT DIE BEFORE IT. There are only FOUR KOLBE DEATHS IN ALL ENGLAND AND WALES BETWEEN 1837 AND 1867 — John Gottlob 1845, George 1848, Elizabeth 1852 and CHARLOTTE KOLBE AT LAMBETH IN 1867. The single Kolbe in the entire 1851 census is also at Lambeth. If the 1867 death is hers she outlived her father by twenty-two years and was simply not caught by the 1851 enumerator under this surname. 20 SEPTEMBER 2026 — SHE IS NO LONGER AN INFERENCE. This record was marked `inf` because she matched no baptism in the family’s own register run and her place in the house was read off a census that records no relationships. MSB 751, her father’s letter of 23 August 1830: “CHARLOTTE SENDS YOU AN EVANGELICAL MAGAZINE, with the account of the death of the Rev. W. Orme, late Secretary to the L.M.S.” HER FATHER NAMES HER SENDING A MAGAZINE TO HER BROTHER. She is a daughter of this house on the evidence of the house.

coenraad-johannes-otto-werdmuller.v: Werdmuller van Elgg · D’Elgg · C.J.O. Werdmuller of Burghersdorp
coenraad-johannes-otto-werdmuller.d: 1882 — death notice KAB MOOC 6/9/187, 4160; will MOOC 7/1/431, 102
coenraad-johannes-otto-werdmuller.r: HE IS IN THE CAPE ARCHIVES FROM 1854 TO 1882 AND HE DIED IN 1882, not merely “before February 1884”. Motions in the Supreme Court in 1854, 1855, 1872 and 1873; a trustee in other men’s insolvent estates; and in 1882, GSC 2/1/1/41 no. 60, “CHARLES ANDREW WERDMULLER AND COENRAAD JOHANNES OTTO WERDMULLER TRADING AS C.A. WERDMULLER AND COMPANY” — FATHER AND SON IN BUSINESS TOGETHER, in the year he died. His own death notice and will are both filed and neither is read. THE MAN THE SETTLER’S FOURTH DAUGHTER MARRIED, and until today a bracket after her name. He is at BURGERSDORP in April 1857, standing at a font with AUGUSTA LOUISA KOLBE. He is at Burgersdorp again on 7 JULY 1874, married BY SPECIAL LICENCE by the Rev. William Cromar to ELIZABETH JOHANNA CATHARINE VORSTER — and the Eastern Province Herald prints his name in full as COENRAAD JOHANNES OTTO WERDMULLER D’ELGG, which is the first time this archive has seen the von Elgg written by anyone but a genealogist. He is DEAD by February 1884, when his second son marries as the son of “the late C.J.O. Werdmuller of Burghersdorp”. WHETHER AUGUSTA LOUISA WAS DEAD BEFORE 1874 THIS ARCHIVE DOES NOT KNOW.

hits.title: The Kolbes
hits.text: That was decisive but it was a single word on a single record. This is a household — a father, a mother, eight fonts in three towns, and three of the children turning up together at the far end. Names can be coincidence. A family moving is not. 1918, four months apart Daniel Jakobus Kolbe , born 3 May 1893, died 19 June 1918 at Wakkerstroom, aged 25. Frederik Fortunatus Downing Kolbe , born 1891, died 2 November 1918 at Wakkerstroom, aged 27. Two brothers, four months apart, in the year of the influenza. Their father outlived them both by thirty-six years.

david-kolbe-booyzen.r: Carries the Kolbe name three generations after the 1820 Settler — AND HE HYPHENATED IT. The family tree recorded his wife Maria Jacoba Smit, married 1921, under the compound surname KOLBE-BOOYSEN, and this archive filed that as a tree oddity with nothing behind it. The Eastern Province Herald prints it twice. 16 OCTOBER 1944: “SAWTELLE – KOLBY-BOOYSEN. The engagement has been announced between LEVINA (FINNIE), only daughter of Mr and Mrs D. KOLBE-BOOYSEN, of PORT ELIZABETH, to Raymond Patrick, only son of Mrs D. Sawtelle, of Cambridge, England.” 19 APRIL 1945: “KOLBE-BOOYSEN – KRUGER. To be married at St Cuthbert's Church, Bingley Street, Port Elizabeth… Hilda, only daughter of Lieut. and Mrs F. Kruger of Heidelburg, Transvaal, to WILLIAM (S.A.A.F.), son of Mr and Mrs D. KOLBE-BOOYSEN, of Port Elizabeth.” A TOWN AND TWO CHILDREN, from two notices six months apart — and the engagement spells the headline KOLBY and the body KOLBE, four words from each other.

david-schalk-booijsen.r: First on his father's 1876 death notice, and a major — and now with a date. His baptism of 4 JANUARY 1807 names his parents as PIETER JACOBUS BOOIJZEN and ANNA MARIA VAN DER MERWE, which is the only document in this archive that puts Anna Maria in the family at all. His father was eighteen when he was born. He married ADRIANA CHRISTINA VILJOEN — on 3 NOVEMBER 1828 AT CRADOCK, a date and a place this archive did not have until WikiTree was read on 13 September 2026, and FROM WIKITREE, NOT FROM A DOCUMENT THIS ARCHIVE HAS READ — and named a daughter ANNA MARIA in 1835, after his own mother. His nephew, born 1848, carries the same name — the two are told apart only by a generation.

david-schalk-booysen.r: PRISONER OF WAR. A printed transport list in the Pretoria government archives, image group 008019246, carries THREE CONSECUTIVE BOOYZENS shipped on the CITY OF CAMBRIDGE on 3 JUNE 1901, all entered from PRETORIA: 18463 STEPHANUS FRANCOIS, 28 · 18464 PETRUS JACOBUS, 29 · 18465 DAVID SCHALK, 54. Consecutive numbers on one transport means taken together. Age 54 against a birth of 9 June 1848, which would have made him 52 and six days short of 53 when the ship sailed. THE FULLER REGISTER WAS THEN FOUND, and it is better than the De List in every respect: item 1 of the same film, image 126, gives all three as living at PRETORIA, riding with the PRETORIA COMMANDO, and TAKEN AT TOLOSBERG ON 25 APRIL 1901. Its ages are 26, 27 and 53, which match this archive's own dates where the De List's 28, 29 and 54 did not. If it is him, he was a Transvaal burgher in arms at fifty-two, taken and deported, and he came back — he remarried at Pretoria in November 1905. Fourth on the 1863 list, and THE DIRECT ANCESTOR'S BROTHER — Willem Hermanus is sixth on the same list. For the whole of this project he was a line on that list and nothing else. His wife's 1900 death notice gives him a household: married ELIZABETHA MARGARETHA MARAIS at LADY GREY, the same small Cape church where his brother married Kathleen Barry in 1879; eight children; and by 1900 he was at Pretoria, living in a zinc building in Market Street. He signed her notice there in March 1904 — and on 27 NOVEMBER 1905 he married again at Pretoria, to JOHANNA ELENA STOLS, widow Lowies, of Skinners Court. He was 56, a widower of GOEDE HOOP, PRETORIA, and the register gives his birthplace as CRADOCK. The Remarks column cites his remarriage certificate from the Master, NO. 4795 — which is the number of his first wife’s death notice, so the two documents point at each other and the identification needs no inference. His own death is still not found.

hits.title: The documents
hits.text: That is one author being consistent with himself, not two sources agreeing, and it is worth exactly that much. And the parents do not agree with the tree This archive has carried, flagged as coming from WikiTree and not from a document, that Anna Maria was a daughter of David Schalk van der Merwe and Anna Elizabeth Louw , born 1785. De Villiers makes her a daughter of Willem van der Merwe and Hester Maria van der Merwe , baptised 1788. Both cannot be right. Neither is being adopted over the other here. But look at what survives the disagreement. On the tree’s version, David Schalk is her father . On de Villiers’s, David Schalk is her brother .

diederik-arnoldus-booysen.r: A KARWEIER — a transport rider — of Zwartruggens, and a son of Ockert Johannes Stephanus Booysen and Elizabeth Johanna Sophia Myburgh. His Sterfkennis 87882 is the first document in this archive printed in Afrikaans rather than Dutch or English, and the first Booysen estate here worth more than £300. He married Elizabeth Anna Bronkhorst, widow Joubert, in community of property; their youngest son carries his grandfather’s name.

Read the two men together: David Schalk Booijzen born Cradock 9 June 1848 and widowed at Pretoria in 1900; Charles Petrus Barend Lowies born district Cradock about 1849 and dead at Pretoria in 1905. Two men born a year apart in one Karoo district, both ending in Pretoria — and five months and twenty-two days after the second died, the first married his widow.

elizabeth-johanna-du-toit.v: Elizabeth Geertruida du Toit, once, at the Hopetown font in 1870
elizabeth-johanna-du-toit.r: FREDERIK FORTUNATUS KOLBE'S WIFE, and the mother of the Settler's Colesberg grandchildren — a woman this archive did not know existed until the index was asked for a relationship rather than a person. She is named at eight fonts across eighteen years and three churches, and her name holds steady at every one but Hopetown. NOT YET FOUND: her marriage and her parents. 17 SEPTEMBER 2026 — HER DEATH IS FOUND, AND SO IS A BIRTHPLACE NOBODY HAD. Pietermaritzburg estate files: “ELIZABETHA JOHANNA DU TOIT KOLBE, BORN 1845 BREDARSDORP K PROVINSIE, DIED 12 JULY 1923, SAXONY UTRECHT NATAL”, probate 1923 — FamilySearch 1:1:QLRL-HRQV. SHE DIED ON A FARM ON THE NATAL BORDER, six years before her husband, SEVEN HUNDRED MILES FROM THE BREDASDORP SHE WAS BORN IN. Her estate names the same nine children as his. THE FILE ITSELF IS NOT READ.

hits.title: The documents
hits.text: The method → 1923 and 1929 · Two estate files at Pietermaritzburg name nine children, and the daughters by their married names This archive knew that Frederik Fortunatus Kolbe , the Settler’s tenth child, married Elizabeth Johanna du Toit and baptised eight children between Colesberg, Hopetown and Bethulie; and that three of them turned up at Wakkerstroom , four hundred miles north. It had no death for either parent and had followed three of the children nowhere at all. The Natal estate index answers all of it in one search.

hits.title: Errands
hits.text: NAB MSCE 8509/1923 and 15161/1929 — ELIZABETH JOHANNA KOLBE, BORN DU TOIT, and FREDERICK FORTUNATUS KOLBE THE COUPLE THIS ARCHIVE DERIVED FROM BAPTISM REGISTERS, CONFIRMED FROM THE OTHER END. Frederik Fortunatus Kolbe, born Bethulie 1839, the Settler's tenth child, married Elizabeth Johanna du Toit — and both their estates are in Natal. His file is cross-referenced to hers in the index. WANTED: his death notice, which should name HIS parents and settle whether the Natal Kolbes descend from the Settler. A seventh is worth adding if anyone is already in the building: NAB MSCE 4064/1974, BOOYZEN, NICOLAAS THEODORUS, BORN IN WAKKERSTROOM.

elizabeth-kolbe-of-westminster.r: Father John, mother Mary. AND SHE MARRIED: Westminster Marriages, 1817, ST CLEMENT DANES — ELIZABETH KOLBE AND JOHN MILNE, both of that parish. She was twenty-one. 20 SEPTEMBER 2026 — AND HER FATHER SAYS WHERE SHE WENT, AND WHAT SHE WAS CALLED. MSB 751, 23 August 1830: “MILNE with ELIZABETH & family had transferred their residence to EDINBURGH; Milne has just come to London on the way of his business, he says that BETSEY likes the situation very well, & they think that they will settle there rather than in London; Milne & Betsey desire their best to you.” THIRTEEN YEARS AFTER THE WEDDING, A MARRIED WOMAN WITH A FAMILY IN SCOTLAND — and a nickname, which no register ever gives. An Elizabeth Kolbe died in the Strand district in 1852, which is the parish next to St Clement Danes; the connection is not made here.
elizabeth-kolbe-of-westminster.tree: That the Elizabeth Kolbe who died in the Strand in 1852 is this woman. Only the district suggests it.

elizabetha-margaretha-marais.r: His wife, married at Lady Grey near Aliwal North. Daughter of STEPHANUS FRANCOIS MARAIS and ELIZABETHA MARGARETHA MARAIS, born in the district of Cradock about April 1850. She died in a ZINC BUILDING IN MARKET STREET, PRETORIA on 1 June 1900 — four days before Lord Roberts entered the town — and her husband did not file the notice for three years and nine months. Nothing movable left, and a compensation claim filed.

hits.title: Disputed
hits.text: If he is David Schalk Booijzen’s son, that boy is called after his grandfather outright; under the reading this archive published, he is called after a great-uncle. Two of the eleven — Ewert Philippus and Susanna Fredrika Aletta — are called straight after his WIFE’S parents, Evert Philip Boshoff and Susanna Frederika Aletta Meyer, which shows this couple did name children after grandparents. The naming argues for the new reading: her father was STEPHANUS FRANCOIS MARAIS, which is exactly where the forename would come from, and there is no Stephanus Francois anywhere in the Pretorius side.

francis-mccabe.d: 23 Feb 1872, the Modder River road, district Bloemfontein
francis-mccabe.r: THE SECOND HUSBAND, and the reason the Commandant's widow is filed under the wrong surname in the Free State estate index. LANDDROST OF BLOEMFONTEIN, son of DR PATRICK McCABE, a Staff-Assistant Surgeon attached to the British Army on the Cape Frontier; his mother ROSE died at Bloemfontein on 1 August 1858, aged 72 years 3 months and 8 days. He married Anna Jacoba van der Merwe about APRIL 1871 — “his second wife, about ten months since” — and was dead within fifteen months. ON THE ANNIVERSARY OF THE STATE'S INDEPENDENCE he had spent the day superintending the burghers' annual target shooting for the government prize; at a quarter past five he set off by spring-cart for the Diamond Fields meaning to sleep at his own farm “UITVLUGT” on the Modder River; at about half past seven, in deceptive moonlight and one hour's ride short of the farm of G.F. Enslin, the cart went into a sluit washed out by the rains. He was dead of heart disease that evening. HE LEFT FOUR SONS AND TWO DAUGHTERS OF HIS OWN AND “A LARGE FAMILY OF STEP-CHILDREN”, which is a newspaper counting the Commandant's twelve. His brother JOSEPH, the well-known trader and traveller, had died in the interior in December 1865; his brother JOHN died at Bloemfontein in 1860. He was buried on the Sunday afternoon at six o'clock, the coffin carried by the resident members of the Volksraad and the principal government officers, with the State President and upwards of two hundred walking behind. 15 SEPTEMBER, FROM THE FREE STATE ESTATE INDEX. VAB MHG C129: “MCCABE, FRANCIS. EGGENOTES 1) MARIA PETRONELLA ELISABETHA ANTOINETTA RAATH EN 2) ANNA (GEBORE VAN DER MERWE)”, 1872 — SO HE HAD A FIRST WIFE AND SHE HAS A NAME. And VAB 1/3/1/12 BC11: “MCCABE, FRANCIS. INSOLVENTE BOEDEL”, with the remark “BEVAT GEEN STERFKENNIS NIE” — CONTAINS NO DEATH NOTICE. The Landdrost of Bloemfontein, buried with the State President walking behind him and two hundred people after that, LEFT AN INSOLVENT ESTATE. His widow's own entry, M777, names both her husbands, so the remarriage is in the archives and not only in a newspaper.

Stepmother and daughter-in-law out of the same family. A fourth Frederik Fortunatus. This one is born 1857 at Bloemfontein and dead there in 1930 . hits.title: The forenames
hits.text: This archive keeps the two apart, and says which is which. One name, three surnames, no blood tie proved between two of them Fortunatus It comes out of the London Kolbes and ends up on a Booÿsen born in the year the war began. Who When What they are to the name Frederik Fortunatus Kolbe of the London Kolbes The source of the name. Frederick Fortunatus Barry — Carried into the Barrys by the Kolbe marriage of 1850. Frederik Fortsenatus Booÿsen b. 1899 And into the Booysens, spelled with a diaeresis, in 1899. Ruben, a Schoeman name, travels the same way into the Barrys — Ruben Jacobus Josuah Barry. Two daughters, one name, eleven months apart The two Gertrudes Not a duplicated record. Two children, two death certificates, two cemeteries.

frederick-fortunatus-kolbe-of-colesberg.r: A CHILD OF FREDERIK FORTUNATUS KOLBE AND ELIZABETH JOHANNA DU TOIT THAT NO FONT IN THIS ARCHIVE RECORDS. Pietermaritzburg estate files — “FREDERICK FORTUNATIS KOLBE, BORN 1872 COLESBERG, DIED 10 SEPTEMBER 1944 VRYHEID”, probate 1944, FamilySearch 1:1:QPHZ-2361 — and he is named as an heir on his mother’s 1923 estate, 1:1:QLR2-5CF4. HIS BIRTH YEAR FALLS IN THE ONE GAP IN HIS PARENTS’ RUN, between Margaret Harriet at Hopetown in 1870 and Catharina Maria Louisa at Colesberg in 1873. He carries his father’s name entire, which is what a family does with a son born after two daughters. THE COLESBERG REGISTER HAS NOT BEEN CHECKED FOR HIS FONT and the estate file is not read.

frederick-fortunatus-werdmuller.r: THE FORTUNATUS NAME IN A FOURTH SURNAME. “PETITION OF FREDERICK FORTUNATUS WERDMULLER OF MALMESBURY”, Cape Supreme Court, 1907, twice in one year, both times in other men's insolvent estates; and an estate of his own in 1953. This archive has already followed FREDERIK FORTUNATUS from Kolbe (1839) to Barry (1863) to Booÿsen (1899); here it is again, on a Werdmuller — and Augusta Louisa Kolbe married a Werdmuller. 17 SEPTEMBER 2026 — HE IS SHOWN TO BE HER SON, AND THE SENTENCE ABOVE IS WITHDRAWN. The last 214 images of the Burgersdorp baptism register hold his font: FREDRIK FORTUNATUS STEENKAMP WERDMULLER, BORN 25 APRIL 1861, BAPTISED 19 MAY 1861 AT BURGERSDORP, FATHER COENRAAD JOHANNES OTTO WERDMULLER, MOTHER AUGUSTA LOUISA KOLBE — FamilySearch 1:1:6FW6-WXGS, image 673. THE SETTLER’S FOURTH DAUGHTER GAVE HER CHILD HER BROTHER’S NAME, which is how Frederik Fortunatus reached a fourth surname. AND IT DATES AUGUSTA LOUISA: she was bearing her husband’s children in 1861, thirteen years before he married again at Burgersdorp in 1874 — which bears directly on whether Charles Andrew was her son. THE ONE STEP NOT TAKEN: that the child of 1861 is the man of the 1907 petition and the 1953 estate. Both are Frederick Fortunatus Werdmuller at the Cape and the name is rare; the 1907 man is of MALMESBURY and the child was baptised at BURGERSDORP, and no document read here joins them.

frederick-kolbe-of-1816.r: RIGHT SURNAME, RIGHT PARISH, RIGHT DECADE, AND A GAP IN THE FAMILY'S OWN BAPTISM RUN EXACTLY THERE. He is not a brother. His father is GEORGE and his mother ELIZABETH, and his register batch is C72301-7 rather than the family's C15051-2 or C06236-1. HE WAS ONE CLICK FROM BEING MADE AN EIGHTH SON, and what stopped it was reading the parents' names on the transcript instead of the name, place and year in the result list. The same check threw out HENRY KOLBE, baptised at Southwark on 2 February 1800 — father Henry, mother Susannah. AND THE REJECTION TURNED OUT NOT TO BE A DEAD END. Morning Advertiser, 31 DECEMBER 1832: “LEFT HIS HOME, MONDAY, DECEMBER 10, FREDERICK KOLBE, ABOUT 16, DARK HAIR AND EYES, WITH AN IMPEDIMENT IN HIS SIGHT. Any information addressed MRS. KOLBE, NO. 18, GERRARD-STREET, SOHO, will be rewarded; if he will return, will…” — and a boy “about 16” in December 1832 is one baptised in December 1816. GERRARD STREET IS TWO STREETS FROM CHURCH STREET. THERE WERE TWO KOLBE HOUSEHOLDS IN SOHO AT ONCE, and every Soho Kolbe record on this site has to be read against that. Whether the two families were related is not known here.

frederik-fortunatus-downing-kolbe.v: Frederik Fortunetus Daomig Kolbe, on his own marriage entry
frederik-fortunatus-downing-kolbe.r: THE MAN WHO PROVED THE CONVERGENCE. He carries BOTH of this family's Kolbe names at once — FREDERIK FORTUNATUS off his grandfather, DOWNING off a London marriage of 1819 — and a London surname has no business in the eastern Transvaal except through that wedding. Born seventy-two years after it. Married HESTER GERBINA SUSANNA JOUBERT at Volksrust at twenty-one, the clerk writing his second name as “Daomig”. Dead at Wakkerstroom on 2 November 1918, four months after his brother Daniel, which is the influenza.

hits.text: Elizabeth Johanna , baptised at Colesberg in 1876, marries John Charles Pattison there at twenty-one. In both cases the age on the marriage agrees with the font to the year. This is the second proof of the Wakkerstroom connection, and it is the better one. The first was a name: Frederik Fortunatus Downing Kolbe , born at Wakkerstroom in 1891, carrying a London surname that has no business in the eastern Transvaal except through a Shoreditch wedding of 1819. That was decisive but it was a single word on a single record. This is a household — a father, a mother, eight fonts in three towns, and three of the children turning up together at the far end. Names can be coincidence. A family moving is not.

frederik-fortunatus-kolbe.r: THE SOURCE OF THE FORTUNATUS NAME across three families — and, as of 14 September 2026, A MAN WITH A HOUSEHOLD. The Settler's tenth child, born at a mission station the year his father was working the Orange River. He married ELIZABETH JOHANNA DU TOIT, and eight of their children are in the Dutch Reformed registers: baptised at COLESBERG in 1863, 1865, 1868, 1873, 1876 and 1877, at HOPETOWN in 1870, and at BETHULIE in 1881. The eldest is a GEORGE AUGUSTUS, named for the grandfather who had been dead nineteen years. THEN THE HOUSEHOLD GOES NORTH: three of those children marry or die at WAKKERSTROOM in the eastern Transvaal, four hundred miles from the font. That is the second proof of the Wakkerstroom convergence, and it does not depend on a name — it is a family moving. 17 SEPTEMBER 2026 — HE HAS A DEATH, A DISTRICT AND AN ESTATE. Pietermaritzburg estate files: “FREDERICK FORTUNABIS KOLBE, BORN 1839 KAAP PROVINSIE, DIED 23 NOVEMBER 1929 AT UTRECHT”, probate 1929 — FamilySearch 1:1:QLR2-XFJC. NINETY YEARS OLD. AND THE ESTATE NAMES HIS CHILDREN, the daughters under both surnames, which is how a daughter gets followed: George Augustus, Gabriel Stephanus, Martha Angelina, MARGARET HARRIET KOLBE VAN DER SPUY, FREDERICK FORTUNATUS, CATHARINA MARIA LOUISA KOLBE LOUW, ELIZABETH JOHANNA KOLBE PATTISON, PETRONELLA JACOBA ADRIANA KOLBE BEUKES and ADRIANA HENRIETTA JOHANNA KOLBE OOSTHUIZEN. NINE, NOT EIGHT — the note above is careful and says eight are in the REGISTERS; the ninth is not. THE FILE ITSELF IS NOT READ.

g-a-kolbe-of-piet-retief.v: almost certainly GEORGE AUGUSTUS KOLBE, the Settler's twin son
g-a-kolbe-of-piet-retief.r: A DATE FOR THE TWIN, IF IT IS HIM. The stone at PIET RETIEF reads “VADER EN MOEDER — G.A. KOLBE — GEB. 23 FEB. 1836 — OVERL. 7 JAN. 1913 — A.M. KOLBE — GEB. 4 MEI 1843 — OVERL. 21 SEP. 1907 — VAN HUN KINDERS”. The Settler's ninth and tenth children were TWINS born at BURGERSDORP IN 1836, Charlotte Felicia and George Augustus, and this archive has never had a day for either. A G.A. KOLBE BORN 23 FEBRUARY 1836 IS EXACTLY THE RIGHT MAN IN EXACTLY THE RIGHT YEAR — and it would date his twin sister too. IT IS INITIALS AND A YEAR, NOT A NAME AND A PARENT, and this archive has spent today being careful about exactly this. It would also give the OTHER George Augustus Kolbe — born Burgersdorp 2 October 1861, dead Standerton 1934, buried Wakkerstroom — a plausible father aged twenty-five, which is the shape the eastern Transvaal Kolbes have been missing.

george-augustus-kolbe.r: HIS OBITUARY IS FOUND, eighteen days after the death: Grahamstown Journal, 19 December 1844. “DIED at his Farm, Wirtemberg, near the Orange River, December 1st, THE REV. GEORGE AUGUSTUS KOLBE, aged 44 years, a man possessed of a most amiable temper, and of more than ordinary abilities. HE WAS THE LAST REMAINING OF EIGHT SONS OF JOHN GODLOFF KOLBE ESQ. OF BRUNSWICK-SQUARE, LONDON, has left a WIDOW AND TEN CHILDREN... he having been for many years engaged in RENDERING THEM MEDICAL ADVICE AND ASSISTANCE whenever called upon... HIS DISEASE WAS AN AFFECTION ON THE LUNGS.” EIGHT SONS, seven of them dead before December 1844 and not one in this archive. BRUNSWICK SQUARE, which is not Conduit Street and is a mile and a half from it. A MAN WHO DOCTORED A DISTRICT FOR THIRTY YEARS, where his own death notice says only “Agriculturist”. And a cause of death, after nearly a year ill. The notice also says 44 when he was 41, and ten children when this archive counts eleven living — it is the best kind of source and it is not a register. 1820 Settler — the Nautilus, Owen's party, Algoa Bay 14 Apr 1820. Married at sixteen on a sworn falsehood, AND THE ROLL CARRIES A SECOND ONE: “KOLBE, GEORGE AUGUSTUS 20. CHEMIST. W MARGARET 19”, where he was sixteen and she was sixteen. HE SAILED FROM GRAVESEND FOUR DAYS BEFORE HIS SEVENTEENTH BIRTHDAY. The two lies do not even agree — nobody “twenty-one and upwards” in January 1819 is twenty in December. OWEN'S PARTY WAS 52 PEOPLE, No. 3 on the Colonial Department list, joint-stock and recruited in London, and IT COLLAPSED IN 1821 when Thomas Owen refused to draw rations and left; his brother took over and the party dispersed. He was eighteen, with no leader, no rations and no location, and the next record of him is the Graaff-Reinet mission three years later. Preached across the Orange River. His grandson could not name him in 1915. 15 SEPTEMBER — HE WAS AN LMS MISSIONARY, AND HIS FATHER WROTE TO HIM. The South African Library at Cape Town holds MSB751, the GA KOLBE COLLECTION, donated by Dr Jean Griffiths of Somerset West in 1985: “George Augustus Kolbe, PHARMACIST, 1820 settler, MISSIONARY, married Margaret Downing” and, on a second entry, “George Augustus Kolbe, 1802–44. LMS MISSIONARY.” IT CORROBORATES A MEMORY THIS ARCHIVE PUBLISHED THE SAME MORNING AS AN INFERENCE — John Montgomery's recollection of a BUSHMAN MISSION SCHOOL AT KOOLSKOP about 1824, where Colesberg now stands. Two sources with nothing to do with each other, agreeing. THE COLLECTION IS FOUR PHOTOCOPIED PAGES CONTAINING A LETTER OF 23 AUGUST 1830 FROM JOHAN KOLBE IN LONDON TO HIS SON — the only known document connecting the tailor of Conduit Street to the settler of Colesberg. IT HAS NOW BEEN READ, AND IT DOES NOT CARRY A STREET ADDRESS. THE CATALOGUE CALLED IT A LETTER “ON HIS ORDINATION” AND THIS ARCHIVE REPEATED THE CATALOGUE; IT IS NOT. 20 SEPTEMBER 2026 — AND A SECOND ATTACHMENT CAME WITH IT. A two-page Afrikaans typescript headed “MSB 751 / [Konsep] vir DSAB / VOORLOPIGE TEKS”, initialled KS and dated 18/2/92 — A DRAFT ENTRY FOR THE DICTIONARY OF SOUTH AFRICAN BIOGRAPHY, BY DR KAREL SCHOEMAN, on the word of the National Library that holds the file: “the author, KS, would be Dr. Karel Schoeman who worked here at the National Library”. IT IS A SECONDARY WORK AND THIS ARCHIVE DOES NOT TAKE SECONDARY WORKS AS EVIDENCE — BUT IT AGREES WITH THIS ARCHIVE ON NINE POINTS REACHED BY NINE OTHER ROADS (the 1802 birth, J.G.E. Kolbe 1822–68 at Leeuberg as a commandant, Margaret Downing 1803–1867, the 1819 London marriage, the apothecary’s trade, the farm Wurthemberg, ten children, Philippolis from March 1831) AND IT IS WRONG ABOUT EXACTLY ONE THING: it calls his father A GERMAN APOTHECARY. He was a tailor, on 121 rate books, two printed masters’ lists, three Gazette notices, the census, the burial register and his other son’s sworn deposition. THE TRADE IS THE SON’S, MOVED ONE GENERATION UP. WHAT THE ENTRY ADDS, ALL OF IT UNTESTED: the GRAAFF-REINET MISSIONARY SOCIETY from about 1824, WORKING AMONG THE SLAVES of the district; acceptance as an LMS MISSION ASSISTANT ON 8 FEBRUARY 1828 and posting to BOESMANSKOOL — THE PRESENT BETHULIE — with JAMES CLARK among the SAN; a journey with MELVILL to the CALEDON VALLEY IN NOVEMBER 1828, as far as present-day Ladybrand, THE EARLIEST JOURNEY IN THE PRESENT FREE STATE OF WHICH A WRITTEN RECORD SURVIVES, and PRINTED UNDER HIS OWN NAME in the Transactions of the Missionary Society for 1829 — a second document he wrote himself, SEARCHED FOR AND NOT FOUND; PHILIPPOLIS from March 1831, alone after Melvill left in March 1832; ORDINATION ON 25 MAY 1833 BY THE FRENCH MISSIONARIES ARBOUSSET AND CASALIS; his advice behind the Berlin Missionary Society’s founding of BETHANIE in 1834; AN ACCUSATION OF ADULTERY IN 1836 with the wife of one of his congregation, agitated by H. HENDRICKS, secretary of the Griqua Council — AN INQUIRY BY THE FRENCH MISSIONARIES ACQUITTED HIM — continued opposition from T. ATKINSON, withdrawal from the station in MARCH 1837 and DISMISSAL BY THE LMS ON 19 JUNE 1837; and the farm DRIEFONTEIN near Philippolis. IT IS ALSO WRONG A SECOND TIME, AND IN ITS OWN FIRST SOURCE: it says his death notice records only eight children. THE DEATH NOTICE NAMES TEN, and this archive has read it, photographed it and published the transcription — KAB MOOC 6/9/35: 7698, signed M. Kolbe at Colesberg in January 1845. IT ALSO SETTLES THE FARM NAME. This archive had WIRTEMBERG from the obituary and KNAPDAAR from the death notice and had quietly run them into one address; “WURTHEMBERG, SOMETIMES ALSO GIVEN AS KNAPDAAR” is the statement that assumption needed. AND IT NAMES A PORTRAIT: a likeness of him AS A YOUNG MAN, in 1992 with C.J. DU PLESSIS OF RUIGTEVLEI, district Bethulie, reproduced in Olivier (1973); and a CHARLES BELL WATERCOLOUR OF A CHURCH SERVICE AT PHILIPPOLIS IN 1834 WITH KOLBE IN THE PULPIT, in the Africana Museum, Johannesburg. THIS ARCHIVE HOLDS NO LIKENESS OF ANYBODY BORN BEFORE 1850. There may be two of this man. AND HE WROTE SOMETHING ELSE, AND IT IS FINDABLE. The 1829 journal extract the DSAB cites is catalogued under the OTHER man’s name, which is why a search for Kolbe found nothing: “EXTRACTS OF THE JOURNAL OF MESSRS MELVILL AND KOLBE, ADDRESSED TO THE REV. RICHARD MILES, SUPERINTENDENT OF THE SOCIETY’S MISSIONS IN AFRICA, PHILIPPOLIS, 25 NOV. 1828”, in the Council for World Missions archive at SOAS — which is source 4 on the DSAB’s own list, two lines above source 6. An edited version dated 18 November 1828 appears in MELVILL (1829), and the journey is printed entire in KAREL SCHOEMAN (ed.), EARLY WHITE TRAVELLERS IN THE TRANSGARIEP, 1819–1840 (Protea, 2003), p. 30. LEGASSICK QUOTES HIM: on the Caledon they met people with “NO OTHER MEANS OF SUBSISTENCE THAN THE WILD ANIMALS FOUND IN THESE PARTS”. THE FIRST WORDS OF HIS THIS ARCHIVE HAS READ, AND THEY ARE ABOUT FAMINE. AND THE MAN HE ADDRESSED IT TO IS VERY PROBABLY THE MAN WHO CALLED AT HIS FATHER’S HOUSE: Richard Miles was sent to Cape Town to act as DR PHILIP’S SUBSTITUTE while Philip was in England, which puts him at the Cape in 1828 and back in London by 1830. The 1830 letter says only “Mr Miles”, so this is an identification and not a document. 20 SEPTEMBER, LATER — AND THE SOCIETY’S OWN REGISTER HAS HIM, FREE, IN EIGHT LINES. James Sibree, A REGISTER OF MISSIONARIES (LMS, 4th ed. 1923), ENTRY 278: “Was previously connected with the GRAAFF REINET MISSIONARY SOCIETY, and laboured AMONG THE SLAVES around Graaff Reinet. Was ACCEPTED PROVISIONALLY BY MR. MILES, FEB. 8, 1829, which action was CONFIRMED BY THE DIRECTORS, JULY 29, 1829. First laboured with MR. CLARK, at the BUSHMAN STATION, CALEDON RIVER. Thence proceeded to PHILIPPOLIS, arriving there, MARCH 13, 1831. On MAY 26, 1833, he was ordained by the French missionaries, Messrs. LEMUE, PELLISIER, AND ARBOUSSET. His connection was dissolved by the Directors, JUNE 19, 1837.” IT SETTLES MR MILES — the man who called at the tailor’s house in London was no messenger, HE WAS THE OFFICER WHO ACCEPTED HIM — and it explains the father’s adverb, because “provisionally” by Miles and “confirmed” by the Directors is precisely what “FULLY accepted” means. IT DISAGREES WITH THE DSAB on the year of acceptance (1829, not 1828), the day of the ordination (26 May) and the men who performed it (Lemue, Pellissier and Arbousset — no Casalis). AND IT IS WRONG ABOUT A SON. Entry 522 calls FREDERICK WILLIAM KOLBE, the Rhenish then LMS missionary of George and Paarl, “SON OF REV. G. A. KOLBE (No. 278)”, where Schoeman says he was no relation. SCHOEMAN IS RIGHT AND THE SOCIETY’S OWN REGISTER IS WRONG: the arithmetic gave it away — a birth of 3 November 1821 against John Gerson Eliezar’s 7 July 1822, EIGHT MONTHS APART — and three works settled it. The New Catholic Encyclopedia calls his son Monsignor F.C. Kolbe “the son of a WESTPHALIAN (GERMAN) PROTESTANT MISSIONARY”; S2A3 names him FRIEDRICH WILHELM KOLBE, Herero scholar, married at Cape Town in 1849 and at Okahandja by April 1850; and the DSAB had published its own entry on him in 1987. SIBREE HAS TWO KOLBES IN SOUTH AFRICA AND A COMPILER JOINED THEM. AND HIS OWN JOURNALS ARE CATALOGUED, IN LONDON. The Council for World Mission archive at SOAS, item-level: CWM/LMS/05/05/100 — “Extracts from the Journal of JOHN MELVILL AND GEORGE AUGUSTUS KOLBE, during a tour to the north-eastwards of Philippolis, 13–22 NOV 1828”, the manuscript behind the printed extract this archive hunted all morning; /102, extracts at Philippolis 1828–1831; /106, Journal, Philippolis 1831–1834; /108, Journal, Philippolis 6 Oct 1832 – Sep 1833. SIX YEARS OF HIS LIFE IN HIS OWN WRITING, where this archive has held one sentence of his at second hand. AND THE YEAR OF THE ACCUSATION IS ONE BOX: incoming correspondence /044 (1835, which the catalogue says contains him), /046 (1836) and the 1837 file — 1836–1837 IS BOX 15. AND ONE LIKENESS IS CATALOGUED, IN SCOTLAND: University of Edinburgh, Centre for the Study of World Christianity, CSWC 60 — five photograph copies of Bell sketches of African congregations, ITEM 3 “MR. KOLBE… AT PHILIPPOLIS IN 1834”. Edinburgh calls him “a moravian missionary?”, question mark and all; HE WAS LONDON MISSIONARY SOCIETY, and this archive has his father’s letter saying so. The DSAB puts the original watercolour in Johannesburg and never mentions Scotland; Edinburgh never mentions Johannesburg.

hits.title: The Booyzen Archive
hits.text: What was searched → Why this archive exists In 1915 a man at Barkly East filled in his own mother's death notice. Where it asked for her parents' names, he wrote: "Father: Kolbe, thinks James was christian name . Mother: Unknown ." His grandfather was George Augustus Kolbe — who married at sixteen on a sworn lie in Shoreditch, sailed on the Nautilus in 1819 as an 1820 Settler , preached across the Orange River, and named a Karoo farm after the Württemberg his own father had left. His grandmother was Margaret Downing of London.

hits.title: The Barrys
hits.text: The 1820 Settler hypothesis does not survive arithmetic. He was born 8 June 1819 . The settler fleets sailed from late 1819 and reached Algoa Bay from April 1820. He cannot have been born on that voyage. But the family does have a documented 1820 Settler — his own father-in-law, George Augustus Kolbe , who sailed on the Nautilus from Gravesend on 3 December 1819. Inferred The likeliest reading is that a true settler story attached itself to the wrong branch.

hits.title: Method
hits.text: The rule was written for a good reason — to stop John Barry collecting every mention of John Barry Booyzen — and it was implemented as “delete the shorter man” rather than “let the longer name go first”. So the moment anybody added George Augustus Kolbe of Wakkerstroom , George Augustus Kolbe stopped existing as far as the build was concerned. Why it is worth a section The data was never wrong. Every record, every document, every citation was intact and on disk the whole time.

hits.title: Open Questions
hits.text: The single most important unopened door: it indexes Cape (KAB) and Transvaal (TAB) estate files and death notices , which is where a death notice for Willem Hermanus Booyzen would be found. Cape Archives (KAB), Master's Office (MOOC) — one reference is already in hand: MOOC 6/9/35: 7698 (1845) , the estate of George Augustus Kolbe. That one has since been read — it is published in full, and on 20 September it caught an error in a historian’s draft that cites it as his own first source. george-augustus-kolbe-of-bethulie.r: TAKEN PRISONER IN 1901, AGED 32, AT STERKFONTEIN IN THE BETHULIE DISTRICT, AND RECORDED AS A FREE STATER. TNA WO 108/368 folio 581. Sent to Natal. THE SECOND MAN OF THAT NAME IN THE SAME LIST — the first being GEORGE AUGUSTUS KOLBE OF BURGERSDORP, whom this archive identified from the Wakkerstroom stones. Bethulie is on the Orange River, in the country the Settler preached across. AND THIRTEEN YEARS LATER A G. A. KOLBE OF BETHULIE IS PRESIDENT OF THE ORANGE FREE STATE AGRICULTURAL ASSOCIATION. The British press, 26 June to 22 July 1914: “MR. G. A. KOLBE (BETHULIE)” in the delegate list printed by the Daily Telegraph; “MR G. A. KOLBE, PRESIDENT OF THE ORANGE FREE STATE AGRICULTURAL ASSOCIATION AND CHAIRMAN OF THE ORANGE FREE STATE DELEGATION” at the Royal Agricultural Society’s show, in the Western Daily Press, Dundee Courier, Cork Free Press and Exeter and Plymouth Gazette of 2 July; and on 22 July the Daily Malta Chronicle has him sending A TELEGRAM OF RESPECTFUL GREETING TO QUEEN WILHELMINA on the delegation’s behalf. SAME INITIALS, SAME DISTRICT, THIRTEEN YEARS APART — from a prisoner’s number to the head of the Free State’s farmers. NO DESCENT FROM THE SETTLER IS CLAIMED HERE.

george-augustus-kolbe-of-burgersdorp.r: THE SECOND GEORGE AUGUSTUS KOLBE OF WAKKERSTROOM, and the reason this archive had to withdraw a claim within the hour. His stone: “IN LIEFVOLLE HERINNERING AAN ONS OUERS — GEORGE AUGUSTUS KOLBE — GEB. 2 OKTOBER 1861 — OORL. 8 NOVEMBER 1934 — EN SUSANNA MARGARETHA KOLBE — GEB. 26 OKTOBER 1861 — OORL. 28 JULIE 1940 — HULLE RUS.” BORN AT BURGERSDORP, which is where the 1820 Settler is buried and where the Settler's twin son George Augustus was born in 1836; the descent is not documented here and is not claimed. He is buried at WAKKERSTROOM although he died at Standerton, in the same cemetery as the other man of his name, TWO YEARS APART IN BIRTH AND TWENTY IN DEATH. AND THE BIRTH DATE DECIDES THE PRISONER: the 1902 POW record of WO 108/368 gives a George Augustus Kolbe of Wakkerstroom AGED 40, and a man born 2 October 1861 was forty from October 1901 to October 1902, where the other was thirty-nine all year. THE PRISONER IS THIS MAN. 17 SEPTEMBER 2026 — AND NOW HE HAS PARENTS. The last 214 images of the Burgersdorp baptism register, film 008039088, hold his font: BORN 2 OCTOBER 1861, BAPTISED 12 JANUARY 1862 AT BURGERSDORP, FATHER G. A. KOLBE, MOTHER ANNA MARIA VILJOEN — FamilySearch 1:1:6FWF-YVJT, image 685. The stone gave a date and a town and this archive wrote that the descent was not documented; THE REGISTER GIVES HIM A COUPLE. He has two younger siblings in the same book. WHETHER HIS FATHER IS THE SETTLER’S TWIN SON — the G.A. Kolbe born 23 February 1836, who would have been twenty-five — IS THE NEXT STEP AND IS NOT TAKEN HERE. 16 SEPTEMBER 2026 — THE POW ENTRY NOW HAS A FOLIO: TNA WO 108/368 FOLIO 709, the War Office list of Boer prisoners of war numbers 1–32,561, which records him as a TRANSVAALER, residence WAKKERSTROOM, and held in NATAL. He is one of SIX KOLBE MEN in that list, and the only one of the six not in the southern Free State.

hits.title: The documents
hits.text: But the same farm carrying the same surname forty years apart is not nothing. The Settler’s own forenames, twice Two men called George Augustus Kolbe were taken prisoner in the same war — one at Wakkerstroom , one at Bethulie . The Wakkerstroom one was already identified on this site , from the gravestones, before this search was run: George Augustus Kolbe of Burgersdorp, born 2 October 1861 , who was forty from October 1901 to October 1902 where the other Wakkerstroom man of that name, born 29 July 1863, was thirty-nine all year. The folio number is the only thing this sweep added to him. The stones → The Bethulie man is new and unattached. No descent is claimed for him.
