george-augustus-kolbe-of-wakkerstroom.r: THE SETTLER'S GRANDSON, CARRYING HIS NAME ENTIRE, and the man the Wakkerstroom Kolbes descend from. Baptised at Colesberg in the year of his uncle Frederick Fortunatus Barry's birth. Married MARTHA SOPHIA KLOPPER, who was seventeen, about 1885; their eldest, Maria Johanna, was born at Wakkerstroom in 1886. AND HIS STONE SETTLES THE IDENTIFICATION BEYOND ARGUMENT: “VADER — GEORGE AUGUSTUS — GEB. 29 JULIE 1863 — OORL. 28 SEPT. 1954”, which is the COLESBERG FONT DATE TO THE DAY. The 1902 POW record with residence Wakkerstroom is NOT HIS: the other George Augustus Kolbe of that town was born 2 October 1861 and was exactly forty through ten months of 1902, where this one was thirty-nine. Died at Wakkerstroom on 28 September 1954, aged 91, which counts EXACTLY from the Colesberg font: born 29 July 1863, dead 28 September 1954. He outlived two of his sons by thirty-six years.

hits.title: The documents
hits.text: The correction → And the prisoner of war is decided, in the other direction. At breakfast this archive gave the 1902 POW record — WO 108/368 , age 40, residence Wakkerstroom — to the man born in 1863, on the strength of the residence. By lunch it had withdrawn that, because he was thirty-nine. The stones close it: the other George Augustus Kolbe of Wakkerstroom was born 2 October 1861 , and was therefore exactly forty from October 1901 to October 1902 . The prisoner is the elder man. Published, withdrawn and reversed inside one day, and all three are on the corrections page, because a reader is owed the whole of that and not just the answer.

hits.title: Method
hits.text: The rule was written for a good reason — to stop John Barry collecting every mention of John Barry Booyzen — and it was implemented as “delete the shorter man” rather than “let the longer name go first”. So the moment anybody added George Augustus Kolbe of Wakkerstroom , George Augustus Kolbe stopped existing as far as the build was concerned. Why it is worth a section The data was never wrong. Every record, every document, every citation was intact and on disk the whole time.

george-downing-daschner.d: buried 20 Jun 1925, Brixton — D.R. section, grave 4410
george-downing-daschner.r: THREE MONTHS AND FIVE DAYS old — not “0 days”, which is the index's reading and what this archive printed for an afternoon. The Brixton register keeps Years, Months and Days in three columns. Buried 20 June 1925, D.R. section, grave 4410 — seventeen years before his father went into West Park. A TWELFTH CHILD, and not on the 1942 death notice because he was already dead when it was written. The Johannesburg cemetery index has him buried at Brixton on 20 June 1925, the year he was born. He carries George Downing — the sixth Booyzen or Barry forename to cross into this family, and the one that makes the pattern impossible to read as coincidence. FROM AN INDEX, not from an image; the burial register has not been read.

hits.title: The Barrys
hits.text: The Barrys stop being a surname in this archive in 1859 and go on being a set of first names for another eighty years. And a sixth, off the 1942 list The Johannesburg cemetery index carries a George Downing Daschner , buried at Brixton on 20 June 1925, the year he was born. He is not on his father's death notice because he was dead seventeen years before it was written — a twelfth child. George Downing is the name of Kathleen Barry's own grandson, born in 1901, and here it is on an infant in another family in the same decade. A second of the name died in 1998.

hits.title: The Booyzen Archive
hits.text: The women are not. Mountjoy (1838). Barry (1879). Kinnear (1940s). Behind the Barrys, Kolbe — a German tailor's family out of Soho who sailed as 1820 Settlers and named a Karoo farm Wurtemburg . Behind the Kolbes, Downing . That is why David Defranceski's great-grandfather, born on a farm in the Eastern Cape in 1901, was christened George Downing Mountjoy Booyzen . Every one of those forenames is a woman's surname. The women → And it is why the tree folds back on itself: in 1924 George married his own first cousin once removed , so his daughter Catherine descends from one Barry–Kolbe couple twice over. The cousin marriage → Corrections are the most valuable thing anyone can send.

hits.title: Disputed
hits.text: Resolved RESOLVED. His 1845 death notice (estate 7698) and his gravestone both give 1 December 1844, and neither his notice nor his widow’s 1867 notice lists a Julia. Reject the child, keep the date. The same two documents also drop KEETOR PETER BENJAMIN KOLBE, whom the tree gives a 1840 birth — he is in neither list. → George Downing Mountjoy Booyzen (1901–1947) Death dated 21 February 1947, with burial ten months later on 14 December 1947. Resolved RESOLVED by his death notice: he died 11 December 1947 and was buried on the 14th. “21 February” is the date the notice was signed — in 1948. A transcriber merged the two and lost ten months.

hits.title: The documents
hits.text: They are the same woman, and the archive's earlier claim of "two Barry sisters marrying Booysens" is withdrawn . 1947 · George's death notice corrects his own death date Signed by G. Booyzen at Johannesburg on 21 February 1948 under the Administration of Estates Act 1913. Death Notice of George Downing Mountjoy Booyzen , died 11 December 1947 at Forest Hill, Johannesburg. "The day of the decease: On 11th December 1947 " — died at 85 Rheeden St, Forest Hill , Johannesburg. He died on 11 December 1947 — not 21 February 1947. 21 February is the date the notice was signed , and it was signed in 1948 . A transcriber conflated the two and lost ten months.

The most that was remembered of where he came from was that it was not here. A trade, passed down 1840, line 5 — Saddler Documented James Montjoy was a saddler at Cradock. gerrit-jacobus-booysen.d: Aug 1951, Middelburg — the day illegible on the stone
gerrit-jacobus-booysen.r: THE STONE IS NOW READ, and it says more than its index line. “IN DANKBARE HULDE AAN ONS GELIEFDE VADER EN OUPA — GERT JACOBUS BOOYZEN — GEB. 19 JAN. 1870 — OORL. 2_ AUG. 1951 — SY GENADE WAS VIR MY GENOEG.” THE BIRTH DAY MATCHES THIS ARCHIVE EXACTLY, and from a source that is not the death notice it came from: 19 January 1870, cut in granite. THE DEATH IS NOW A MONTH instead of a year — AUGUST 1951 — and the day is a 2 followed by a digit this archive cannot read off the photograph, so it is not guessed. VADER EN OUPA: he was a grandfather, which no document here had said. AND THE LAST LINE IS IN THE FIRST PERSON — “His grace was enough for ME” — a widower’s sentence, cut twenty-one years after his wife died. HIS GRAVE IS PHOTOGRAPHED. The eGGSA gravestone library holds “BOOYZEN GERT JACOBUS 1870-1951” in the MIDDELBURG MAIN CEMETERY, Eastern Cape — born 1870 and dead in 1951, which is the year of estate TAB MHG 5155/51, the file this archive has been trying to read on blocked film. He is buried a few stones from his wife. IMAGE LOCATED, NOT YET READ. The only child entered on his father's 1884 death notice, and born seven years after the first wife died — so a child of the second marriage. He married Isabella Frederika Coetsee at Middelburg on 23 March 1896, and his own son was baptised BOOYZEN, with a z, in 1904.

hits.title: The documents
hits.text: Not one Booysen among them. Two van Stadens — Jacob Alewyn and Coenrad Sybert . Four Rooses — Gert Johannes , Matthys Johannes , Johannes Sybert , and Anna Francisa , married in community of property to Gert Johannes Laubeschagne. All of age. And after ten years of marriage to Hendrik Stefanus Booysen, no child of his is named , because she was fifty-one when she married him. This archive spent a month drawing his four children under her. Earlier today the 1892 marriage register — her age, her condition — made that impossible. Her own death notice now says the same thing from the other side, in her husband’s handwriting.

gerthardus-lodewikus-booysen.r: THE ONE DOCUMENT THAT NAMES HIM HAS BEEN WEAKENED, AND BY SOMEBODY WHO HAD NOT SEEN IT. On 14 September 2026 PIETER VAN ZYL, answering this archive’s G2G question, guessed that the 1876 informant had reached for a name already in the household — and added, from memory, that he thought a CHILD of Petrus Jacobus was called Gerhardus Lodewicus. HE IS RIGHT, AND THE CHILD IS ON THE SAME SHEET: line 12 of that very notice names JAN GERTHARDUS LODEWIKUS BOOIJSEN among the eight children. So the name this archive takes from LINE 3, for the dead man’s FATHER, is the back half of his SON’S name, eight lines below, in one clerk’s hand — and the half that is dropped, JAN, is the name de Villiers gives as the real father. THIS DOES NOT PROVE THE FATHER WAS JAN and this archive is not swapping one unproved father for another. It removes the only document that has ever carried this name from the evidence for him. The top of the male line is now held up by less than it was this morning. He still has no birth date, no death date, and no parents: the oldest open question on this site is about him. 15 SEPTEMBER 2026 — AND THE LAST ESCAPE ROUTE IS CLOSED. This archive's standing objection was that de Villiers's 1893 original was revised by Pama in 1981, and a revision can move a man; if the 1981 edition had relocated Petrus Jacobus, the death notice would stand. RIËL SMIT, WHO HAS THE 1981 EDITION: “Yes, DE VILLIERS & PAMA (1981) STILL PLACE PETRUS JACOBUS (b3c4d7) b. 21 SEPT 1788 UNDER JAN b3c4.” Pieter van Zyl adds that he SEARCHED FOR A MARRIAGE BETWEEN A GERHARDUS LODEWICUS AND A MAGDALENA DE BEER AND COULD NOT FIND ONE. FOUR THINGS NOW POINT ONE WAY and the only thing pointing the other is line 3 of Notice 678. THE SPINE IS STILL NOT BEING MOVED ON THIS: everything against him is a printed genealogy agreeing with its own earlier edition, and what he has is a primary document signed by a son. WHAT ENDS IT IS THE BAPTISM ENTRY OF 21 SEPTEMBER 1788 — the register de Villiers compiled his entry from, naming the father in a contemporary hand. It is now the first item on the errands page.

hits.text: Seven generations up, the male line simply ends. One thing has changed here, and it is worth being precise about how little. Until the 1876 Sterfkennis was read, generation seven existed only because a family tree said so. It now exists because a nineteenth-century clerk wrote "Gerthardus Lödewikus Booijsen" and "Magdalena de Beer" on his son's death notice. hits.title: The documents
hits.text: Not on the 1940 estate because the child was already dead when it was written. FANIE Stephanus Francois Booyzen the younger Fanie ← Stefanus. Standard, and unambiguous. WILLIE Willem Hendrik Booyzen Willie ← Willem PIETIE Petrus Jacobus Booyzen Pietie ← Petrus JOHAN Johan Abraham Frederik Booyzen The same name HENNIE Hendrik Rudolph Philippus Booyzen Hennie ← Hendrik Eleven names on the estate, twelve on the stone, and every one of the eleven is claimed exactly once. That is what makes the twelfth real. Nine of the matches are ordinary Afrikaans diminutives; two — ouboet and ousie — are not names but places in the family, and they fall to the two children the diminutives leave over. Nothing is left unassigned except ✝ BABA .

hendrik-stefanus-booijsen.r: Seventh on the 1876 notice — and the man who signed it, four lines under his own name, beside the veldkornet. His own death notice, TAB estate 14380, names HIS mother as ELIZABETHA BOOYSEN, BORN VAN DER MERWE — which resolves this archive’s oldest “Serious” contradiction, because his father’s recorded wife Anna Maria van der Merwe died three years before he was born. A FARMER, “Dutch”, married twice — Anna Catharina Johanna Olivier, then Charlotta Elizabetha Dormehl — and married last at ZEERUST, in the district of Marico. He died in his son-in-law’s house.

hits.title: Disputed
hits.text: Serious Petrus Jacobus remarried and the second wife is missing from the tree. Two “sons” belong to her. → Anna Maria van der Merwe (1785–1825) Dies before 8 March 1825 — but Hendrik Stefanus is recorded born 23 August 1829. Resolved RESOLVED, 13 September 2026. The second marriage is no longer unrecorded. Hendrik Stephanus Booysen's own 1908 death notice — Transvaal estate 14380 — names his mother as ELIZABETHA BOOYSEN, BORN VAN DER MERWE, and gives his age as seventy-nine years eleven months at 11 May 1908, which puts his birth about June 1828, three years after the first wife died. Two van der Merwe wives in succession. The contradiction was never a contradiction; it was a missing row.

hits.title: What changed
hits.text: She died at Wodehouse on 25 October 1897, aged fourteen months. On 8 November 1901 they had another daughter and gave her the whole name again; she married Hendrik Stefanus Palm, and a granddaughter born in 1920 carries it still. Replacement naming is well attested in these congregations and is exactly how a records-matcher invents one person out of two. The dates here make it unmistakable, and this archive keeps the two apart.

henry-james-booyzen.b: 12 Aug 1887, baptised 27 Nov 1887 at Barkly East
henry-james-booyzen.d: 8 Dec 1956, Florence Nightingale Nursing Home — buried 12 Dec, grave 7110/1
henry-james-booyzen.r: AND NOW THERE IS A REGISTER. The G2G question this archive posted on 13 September was answered within eighteen hours by PIETER VAN ZYL, who put the baptism on the profile: “South Africa, Dutch Reformed Church Registers (Cape Town Archives)”, ark 1:1:6KPT-T3Z4 — HENRY JAMES BOOŸSEN, BORN 12 AUGUST 1887, BAPTISED 27 NOVEMBER 1887, parents WILLEM HERMANUS BOOŸSEN and CATHARINA MARIA SOPHIA BARRY. Verified here against the index directly. The 12 August 1887 has now travelled from a family tree, to a gravestone, to a church register, in that order, which is the wrong way round and is how it usually goes. THE SAME ANSWER ALSO SAYS he was A CARPENTER WHEN HE MARRIED and A RETIRED MINER OF LANGLAAGTE ESTATES when he died, OF PHTHISIS — and this archive has CORONARY PULMONARY SCLEROSIS off the Johannesburg burial register. 17 SEPTEMBER 2026 — THE DOCUMENT IS READ, AND BOTH REPORTS WERE WRONG. His FORM OF INFORMATION OF A DEATH, South Africa Civil Death Registration 1953–1967, film 007751812 image 356, FamilySearch 1:1:6Z9Q-2TFG — the image itself, not the index. PHTHISIS IS ON LINE 11, WHICH IS “PENSIONER OR RECIPIENT OF MAINTENANCE ALLOWANCE”. IT IS NOT HIS CAUSE OF DEATH; IT IS THE ALLOWANCE HE DREW, as a certified miners’ phthisis pensioner. LINE 12, CAUSES OF DEATH, READS “COR PULMONALE WITH SILICOSIS”, with “CONTRIBUTING CAUSE: BRONCHO PNEUMONIA”, after an illness of TWO YEARS and a final SEVEN DAYS. AND THE BURIAL REGISTER’S “CORONARY PULMONARY SCLEROSIS” IS A MANGLING OF THAT SAME LINE — cor pulmonale became coronary pulmonary, silicosis became sclerosis. ONE SHEET OF PAPER, TWO WRONG READINGS, AND THIS ARCHIVE WAS CARRYING BOTH. The form also gives: IDENTITY NUMBER 331-452322; his own DATE OF BIRTH AS 12-8-1887, which is the fourth independent statement of it after a tree, a gravestone and a church register; RESIDENTIAL ADDRESS 3 FIFTEENTH AVENUE, MAYFAIR, JOHANNESBURG — the parish where his niece married Nuno Lerena seven years earlier; place of birth CAPE PROVINCE; medical practitioner DR A. L. AGRANAT; and an informant at 6 JORISSEN STREET, BRAAMFONTEIN described only as “PERSON CAUSING BURIAL”, which the form distinguishes from a relative. AND HIS STONE SETTLES THE BIRTH. WEST PARK, Johannesburg: “HIER RUS — MY DIERBARE EGGENOOT — HENRY JAMES — GEB. 12.8.1887 — OORL. 8.12.1956 — RUS IN VREDE”, over the surname BOOYZEN. The 12 August 1887 this archive carried marked FROM WIKITREE AND NOT FROM A DOCUMENT is now on his own gravestone, and the death matches the burial register to the day. “My dierbare eggenoot” — the stone was raised by his widow, Dorothea Regina. HIS GRAVE IS PHOTOGRAPHED: “BOOYZEN HENRY JAMES 1887-1956”, WEST PARK CEMETERY, Johannesburg — matching the burial register this archive read and the 12 August 1887 birth WikiTree gives. IMAGE LOCATED, NOT YET READ. A son of Willem Hermanus and Kathleen Barry. WikiTree gives his birth as 12 AUGUST 1887 and his marriage as 17 JUNE 1912 AT ELLIOT, neither of which this archive had—bothFROM WIKITREE, NOT FROM A DOCUMENT THIS ARCHIVE HAS READ, and the “c. 1887” below is this archive’s own figure, worked back from an age on a burial register. This archive had him as a name on Transvaal estate MHG 10/57 and nothing else — not a birth, not a death. The Johannesburg cemetery register gives all of it: DIED 8 DECEMBER 1956 at the FLORENCE NIGHTINGALE NURSING HOME of CORONARY PULMONARY SCLEROSIS, aged 69, usual residence 3 15TH AVENUE, MAYFAIR — the same suburb where his mother died in 1940 and where his great-niece was married at St Joseph’s in 1949. Buried 12 December in the D.R. section, GRAVE 7110/1, a double plot. In 1912 he married Dorothea Regina Barry, a daughter of his mother's brother Hendrik Nicholaas — the third Barry–Booyzen union in three generations.

henry-james-kolbe-barry.r: NEW, AND HE CARRIES THE WHOLE ARGUMENT IN HIS NAME. “BARRY, HENRY JAMES KOLBE. BORN IN BARKLY EAST, CAPE PROVINCE. UNMARRIED. DECEASED ESTATE”, Pietermaritzburg Archives Repository, MSCE 2183/1958. HENRY JAMES is the Barry forename this archive has followed since 1848; KOLBE is the surname it has spent the project proving is the source of half the family's given names. HERE THEY ARE IN ONE MAN, born in this archive's own town, dying UNMARRIED in Natal in 1958 — so the names stop with him. He is the third Barry found carrying Kolbe as a forename, after Richard Pieter Kolbe Barry and Anton Rector Kolbe Barry. NO PARENTS NAMED; the estate is not read.

hits.title: What changed
hits.text: Whether it was DELIVERED is a separate question from whether it was sent, and this archive will not use the second word until it has checked for the first. A dead child's name, given again — watched happening Found found Worked out of the register rather than off a new document. Hercules Johannes Mountjoy and Maria Sophia van Niekerk baptised a daughter at Dordrecht on 6 September 1896 and called her CAROLINA ISABELLA MARGARETHA ALETTA, her grandmother's four names entire. She died at Wodehouse on 25 October 1897, aged fourteen months.

hits.title: The documents
hits.text: And the Keys question is answered. This site has carried a William Henry Keys who married a Johanna Catharina Mountjoy and baptised children at Dordrecht, Burgersdorp and Barkly East between 1878 and 1898 — among them James Jonathan Keys and Herklaas Edward Johannes Keys , Mountjoy forenames crossing into a third surname. It has been asking which Johanna Catharina Mountjoy. This one. The Keys marriage record estimates her birth at 1859 ; the Burgersdorp font gives 28 January 1860 . She is George Mountjoy’s daughter , and the Mountjoy forenames that turn up in the Keys children are her father’s and her brother’s.

hermanus-pietersen.r: ANNA CATHARINA SLIER'S FIRST HUSBAND, AND UNTIL TODAY THIS ARCHIVE HAD HIM AND HIS SON AS ONE MAN. De Villiers, volume 3: “HERMANUS PIETERSEN, NAMEN VAN OUDERS ONBEKEND, gehuwd 5 APRIL 1807 met ANNA CATHARINA SLIER — (b) 1 Willem Hermanus, gedoopt 12 Maart 1809; 2 Johan Christiaan, gedoopt 28 April 1810.” The entry here used to read “Willem Hermanus Pieterzen, her first husband”, built from two documents that spell him differently — the 1817 marriage register's HARMANUS PIETERZE and the 1840 death notice's WILLIAM PIETERSEN — and two spellings looked like one long name. THEY ARE A FATHER AND A SON. His own parents were unknown to the book, as James Montjoy's would be to the clerk ten years later: TWO MEN IN ONE WOMAN'S LIFE AND NEITHER OF THEM HAD A RECORDED FATHER.

hits.text: That was wrong, and it was corrected on 15 September 2026. Corrected from the printed genealogy De Villiers gives “Hermanus Pietersen, namen van ouders onbekend, gehuwd 5 April 1807 met Anna Catharina Slier” and their sons as Willem Hermanus (1809) and Johan Christiaan (1810) . The husband is Hermanus ; the 1851 godfather is his son , which this page already said in the line above without following it. The 1840 notice is the odd one out.

hits.text: A third indexing, under the spelling Montyoy , did. Graaff-Reinet marriage register, folios 60–61. "Den 9 Maart 1817 getrouwd" — married on 9 March 1817. The entry, with a pencil cross beside it: "James Montjoy — Met · Anna Catharina Slier, weduwe van Harmanus Pieterze[n]" What it does not say, and that is the point This archive went to this register expecting an origin . Cape marriage entries of this date routinely record where a party came from, and this very page does it repeatedly — three couples in the right-hand column are entered "beide van Uitenhage" . Against James Montjoy's name there is a long ruled dash and nothing else .

hits.title: The Name
hits.text: Five spellings of one woman are a fact about handwriting. Two spellings of one surname are supposed to be a fact about history. The difference is that somebody in this family cared about the second one. And the same page gives the other half of the pattern. Her son was baptised Willem Hermanus Pietersen in 1809; the 1851 Graaff-Reinet register writes the surname Pieterzen , twice, in the hand that wrote Booyzen three lines above. The Pietersens changed nothing either. What the name means A patronymic Booysen is Dutch and means "son of Booy" . Booy is itself a short form of Boudewijn — the Dutch form of Baldwin , from Germanic bald ("bold") and win ("friend").

james-henry-barry.v: Henry Jaonas Barry · Hennery James Berry (both 1848 index entries)
james-henry-barry.r: SETTLED, 14 September 2026, and it removes a candidate rather than adding one. The HENRY JAONAS BARRY who turned up on 13 September — “baptised at twenty years old” in 1868, and briefly a candidate for a tenth child — IS THIS MAN. The same event is indexed twice: once as Henry Jaonas Barry, baptism 13 Nov 1868, and once as HENNERY JAMES BERRY, baptism 13 Nov 1848. Same birth date of 13 July 1848, same parents, same collection, and FamilySearch attaches BOTH to one tree person, James Henry Barry 1848–1939. The volume decides the year on its own: the register is “GRAAFF-REINET. BAPTISM RECORDS 1846–1851”, and a baptism of 1868 cannot sit in a book that closes in 1851. So he was baptised at four months, not at twenty, AT GRAAFF-REINET — not at Cape Town or Tulbagh, which is what both index entries say for the place. The birth-spacing argument made against him held: his brother John Augustus II was born 13 March 1847 and he was born sixteen months later. THE IMAGE HAS BEEN LOCATED AND NOT READ — identifier apid:TH-909-70517-31299-17. Named on the 1915 death notice, which he swore himself. The index now dates him: born about 1847, dead at Barkly East on 23 June 1939, having outlived his father by thirty-six years. BUT THAT YEAR CANNOT STAND. His brother John Augustus Barry II was born 13 MARCH 1847 off a register, and “about 1847” here is not a date at all — it is an age worked back from the 1939 death. Two brothers cannot share it. A relationship search on his mother's surname turned up a HENRY JAONAS BARRY born 13 July 1848 and baptised at twenty, which is where a next child belongs; whether that is this man under a clerk's ear is UNPROVED and the register is unread.

hits.title: The documents
hits.text: And the Keys question is answered. This site has carried a William Henry Keys who married a Johanna Catharina Mountjoy and baptised children at Dordrecht, Burgersdorp and Barkly East between 1878 and 1898 — among them James Jonathan Keys and Herklaas Edward Johannes Keys , Mountjoy forenames crossing into a third surname. It has been asking which Johanna Catharina Mountjoy. This one. The Keys marriage record estimates her birth at 1859 ; the Burgersdorp font gives 28 January 1860 . She is George Mountjoy’s daughter , and the Mountjoy forenames that turn up in the Keys children are her father’s and her brother’s.

james-montjoy.r: Saddler. Owned a house and erf at Cradock worth £90. His 1840 death notice gives his parents as NOT KNOWN — the oldest document here, and the top of this line. 15 SEPTEMBER 2026 — A MAN WHO SLEPT IN HIS HOUSE SAYS WHERE HE CAME FROM. John Montgomery, founder of Burgersdorp, in The Friend of the Free State of 25 November 1869, recalling his arrival at Cradock in January 1822 when the place held about six people: “Messrs. SOLOMON and S.M. DE BEER, the Rev. Mr. EVANS, Mr. P. GIE, JAMES MOUNTJOY (A SADDLER, WHO WAS DISCHARGED FROM THE 21ST LIGHT DRAGOONS), the two Messrs. ZIERVOGEL, Mr. HEILBERG, Fieldcornet B.J. VORSTER, and Gert VAN DEVENTER. After some trouble I obtained lodgings for the night from Mr. MOUNTJOY.” THERE IS NO ROOM IN A VILLAGE OF SIX FOR TWO SADDLERS OF ONE NAME. The 21st Light Dragoons were the cavalry of the Cape garrison from the 1806 expedition until the end of that decade, so HE ARRIVED IN UNIFORM — which is exactly why no Cape document can say where he was from, and why the marriage register of 1817 rules a line through the column and leaves it empty. He was not a passenger on anything. THE RECORD THAT ANSWERS IT IS WO 97 AT KEW, the Chelsea discharge papers, arranged by regiment before 1855, which give a soldier's PARISH AND COUNTY OF BIRTH, his age at enlistment and his trade. 16 SEPTEMBER 2026 — HIS DISCHARGE NOW HAS A DEADLINE, AND IT CAME FROM THE LONDON PAPERS. The 21st Light Dragoons were relieved at York in MAY 1806 and sailed from Portsmouth for the Cape; part of them went on to SOUTH AMERICA in 1806 and came back to the Cape in 1807; Parliament complained in MARCH 1809 that they had been sent “WHERE THEY COULD HAVE NOTHING TO DO”; a large reinforcement followed in OCTOBER 1810; SIR JOHN CRADOCK reviewed them and pronounced them “IN THE HIGHEST STATE OF DISCIPLINE”; a DRAFT OF 140 MEN embarked for the Cape in OCTOBER 1813; and then, in a letter from the Cape dated 1 AND 10 SEPTEMBER 1817 and printed in five London papers that November, “THE 21ST LIGHT DRAGOONS HAVE EMBARKED FOR INDIA”. HE MARRIED AT GRAAFF-REINET ON 9 MARCH 1817. HIS REGIMENT SAILED FOR INDIA SIX MONTHS LATER. A man who married in March 1817 and was keeping a house and a saddler's trade at Cradock by January 1822 was discharged at the Cape BEFORE SEPTEMBER 1817, and what he was choosing between was a wife at Graaff-Reinet and a transport to Madras. THE TOWN HE SETTLED IN IS NAMED AFTER THE GOVERNOR WHO REVIEWED HIS REGIMENT.

jan-booijsen.r: THE MAN THE BOOK PUTS WHERE THE DOCUMENT PUTS SOMEBODY ELSE. b3c4 — son of Gerrit Booijsen and Johanna du Rand; burgher at Drakenstein; MARRIED MAGDALENA DE BEER 21 JANUARY 1770 and remarried MARGARETHA PRETORIUS 15 DECEMBER 1793, which is how this archive knows the de Beer wife was dead by then. De Villiers (1893) gives him twelve children, of whom d5 is JAN JONATHAN, d6 MAGDALENA and d7 PETRUS JACOBUS, BAPTISED 21 SEPTEMBER 1788 — this archive's own ancestor. RIËL SMIT CONFIRMS THAT DE VILLIERS & PAMA (1981) STILL PLACES HIM THERE. Pieter van Zyl notes he was dead more than forty years before Petrus Jacobus died in 1876, which is why the grandson who signed the death notice could write somebody else's name in the parents' box. HE IS ENTERED AS INFERRED AND NOT AS DOCUMENTED, because two editions of one printed genealogy are one source agreeing with itself, and the primary document on this site says Gerthardus Lodewikus. The baptism register of 21 September 1788 decides between them.

hits.title: What changed
hits.text: The decisive one failed in an informative way: the 1788 baptism that names Petrus Jacobus's father does not surface, because the date filters are ignored and the 18th-century Cape registers are not name-indexed — a negative about the index, not the register. Two other entries independently confirmed de Villiers on two of Jan Booijsen's sons, which strengthens the book against the death notice. And the relationship search on the father, queued as Question 13, returned a household: John Augustus Barry II had a wife and nine children this archive had never seen, including the Kolbe name carried into a fourth generation.

hits.text: This row has deliberately not been changed. Everything against him is a printed genealogy agreeing with its own earlier edition, which is one source agreeing with itself; what he has is a primary document signed by a son. Jan Booijsen is on this site as INFERRED, not documented , and he is not in the table above. What ends it is the baptism entry of 21 September 1788 , which is at Cape Town and is not on FamilySearch — that collection begins in 1843. jan-gerhardus-lodewicus-booysen.r: Seventh on the 1863 list, and carries the name of the man at the top of the line. THIS ARCHIVE HAD HIM DYING IN 1885 AND HAS TAKEN IT BACK: estate TAB MHG O/2899 belongs to his uncle of the same name, born 1818, and the death date was never anything but the estate’s year read backwards onto the wrong man. Nothing is known about what became of him — AND THERE IS NOW ONE PLACE TO LOOK. A JGL BOOYZEN countersigned the money papers of a farm school at KWAGGAFONTEIN, DISTRICT MARICO, through 1898 and into 1899: the subsidy application, the book orders, all four quarterly returns, the writing-off of a £61-6-0 deficit, and a letter arguing that the government had paid £8 too little. The elder man of these initials was thirteen years dead by then. This one would have been forty-two, and Marico adjoins the district his uncle died in. IT IS A CANDIDATE AND NOT AN IDENTIFICATION — the index gives initials, a farm and a post office, and Jan Gerhardus Lodewicus is one of the commonest name-strings in the surname. The file itself would carry a signature.

jan-gerthardus-lodewikus-booijsen.r: Fifth on his father’s 1876 notice, and named for the man at the top of the line. HIS is the estate TAB MHG O/2899, which this archive had spent months attributing to his nephew of the same name born in 1855 — the Transvaal probate index gives him as the deceased, aged 67, born district Graaff-Reinet, died 25 May 1885 at Vaalbank in the district of Lichtenburg. His daughter Magdalena Susanna Maria died on the same farm in 1920, and her death notice names him. He is how this family reaches the western Transvaal.

hits.title: What changed
hits.text: Pieter van Zyl had already searched for a marriage between a Gerhardus Lodewicus and a Magdalena de Beer and found none, and remembered — correctly — that a CHILD of Petrus Jacobus carried the name. He is on line 12 of the same sheet: Jan Gerthardus Lodewikus Booijsen. The name in the parents' box is the back half of a son's name, and the half that was dropped is the father's. BOTH LETTERS WENT OUT THE SAME MORNING: a short thanks to Ms Xaba asking only whether MHG 52653 is a valid reference, and a first approach to the private researcher — what she charges and how, her view on whether the work is worth doing at all, and an offer to start with one file.

hits.title: What changed
hits.text: The date had no source except the file number. The Transvaal probate index names the estate's deceased in full: Jan Gerardus Lodewicus Booijzen, aged 67, born district Graaff-Reinet, died 25 May 1885 at Vaalbank, district Lichtenburg — born about 1818, which is his UNCLE, fifth on the 1876 Sterfkennis. The nephew's death date is withdrawn and nothing is known about what became of him. The particular error is worth naming: the archive read a year off a reference number, wrote it in as a fact, and then cited the fact back.

johan-gottlieb-kolbe.v: John Gottlob · “JOHN GODLOFF KOLBE ESQ. OF BRUNSWICK-SQUARE”, in his son’s 1844 obituary · and twenty-four spellings in the Westminster rate books
johan-gottlieb-kolbe.tree: The 1844 obituary’s “Brunswick-square”. No Westminster rate book, land tax return, census or burial register places him there, and Bloomsbury’s own sources have not been searched.
johan-gottlieb-kolbe.r: HE HAD EIGHT SONS, AND THIS ARCHIVE KNEW OF ONE. His son’s obituary in the Grahamstown Journal of 19 December 1844 calls George Augustus “THE LAST REMAINING OF EIGHT SONS OF JOHN GODLOFF KOLBE ESQ. OF BRUNSWICK-SQUARE, LONDON”. SEVEN BROTHERS, ALL DEAD BEFORE DECEMBER 1844, none of them named anywhere in this archive — and dead men do not appear in a census, which is why the 1841 Conduit Street household holds three women and no sons. THE OBITUARY ALSO PUTS HIM AT BRUNSWICK SQUARE, in Bloomsbury, where the census and the death put him at CONDUIT STREET in Mayfair, a mile and a half away. Both can be true twenty years apart, and this archive has already moved this man once — off the family tree’s Lamb’s Conduit Street — so it records a second address rather than making a second correction. “ESQ.”, not “tailor”. AND HE IS IN THE LONDON GAZETTE, nine years before he died: issue 19424, page 1702, 29 September 1836, dissolving the copartnership of “JOHN GOTTLOB KOLBE and DAVID FLETCHER, of Conduit-Street, Bond-Street, in the County of Middlesex, TAILORS”. That is his trade, his street and a business partner, in print, from a free source — and it pushes him back to Conduit Street in 1836. AND THE DEATH IS NOW A GRO REFERENCE: FreeBMD gives one Kolbe death in all of England and Wales for 1845–46 — “Deaths Dec 1845, KOLBE, JOHN GOTTLOB, ST GEO HAN SQ, VOL 1, PAGE 35”. The district matches the census; the name form JOHN GOTTLOB matches his son's 1803 baptism; and the certificate, not yet ordered, would name the informant. FOUND IN THE 1841 CENSUS, which settles two things this archive had argued from other documents. He is at CONDUIT STREET, St George Hanover Square, sub-district MAY FAIR, aged 76 — four years before he died at number 34, and independent of the death record that corrected the family tree's Lamb's Conduit Street. And his birth county is entered as “FOREIGN”, which is the first document in this archive to say in its own words that he was not English. HO107, piece 734, book 1, folio 11, page 15, SCHEDULE 38. Three women share that schedule: Marianne, 35, Charlotte, 30, and Amelia A., 25. Tailor. Died at 34 Conduit Street, Mayfair — not Lamb's Conduit Street; the tree's photograph is of the wrong building. 16 SEPTEMBER 2026 — THE ADDRESS ARGUMENT IS OVER, AND HE HAD TWO WIVES. The WESTMINSTER RATE BOOKS index him ONE HUNDRED AND TWENTY-ONE TIMES between 1800 and 1831, under TWENTY-FOUR SPELLINGS of his forename — Gothel, Gotleb, Gotleib, Gotlieb, Gotliel, Gotlob, Gotlobe, Goltief, Gottieb, Gottiel, Gottlieb, Gottlob, Gutlieb, Kottieb, Gilliet and once “Jos Gottiel”. In 1800 he is at BROAD STREET NORTH, St James Piccadilly, folio 41 — which independently corroborates the printed 1799 list of 234 master tailors, “Kolbe, John, 18 Broad-street, Soho”. From 1811 to 1831 he is at CHURCH STREET SOUTH, ST ANNE’S SOHO, year after year, and the 1829 land tax return says the same. BRUNSWICK SQUARE APPEARS IN NO RATE BOOK, NO LAND TAX RETURN, NO CENSUS AND NO BURIAL REGISTER — those are Westminster sources and Bloomsbury would not be in them, so they cannot disprove it, but Soho 1800–1831, St George Hanover Square in 1841 and a death there in 1845 leaves no window for it. AND THE BURIAL IS NOW A REGISTER ENTRY RATHER THAN A TREE CLAIM: Westminster Burials, City of Westminster Archives Centre — DIED 18 NOVEMBER 1845, BURIED 26 NOVEMBER 1845 AT ST JOHN THE BAPTIST, GREAT MARLBOROUGH STREET, page 7, year of birth given as 1764. The date matches the tree’s “26 November 1845, entry 55, grave 7” to the day and the “7” matches; the church does not. 20 SEPTEMBER 2026 — HE WRITES, AND HE SIGNS HIMSELF. MSB 751 at the National Library of South Africa is a letter of FOUR SIDES headed “LONDON AUGUST 23. 1830”, opening “DEAR GEORGE” and signed “YOUR AFFECTIONATE FATHER, J G KOLBE”. IT IS THE FIRST DOCUMENT IN THIS ARCHIVE HE WROTE HIMSELF — everything else is somebody writing about him. IT DOES NOT CARRY A STREET ADDRESS: the heading is “London” and nothing finer, so it does NOT settle Brunswick Square against Conduit Street, which is what this archive most hoped for. WHAT IT DOES CARRY: his son’s acceptance by the LONDON MISSIONARY SOCIETY in the father’s own words, DR PHILIP carrying an earlier letter to the Cape, MR MILES of the Society calling at the house, HENRY dying of DROPSY and “resigned to the Catastrophe”, MILNE AND ELIZABETH — “Betsey” — removed to EDINBURGH, CHARLOTTE sending an Evangelical Magazine, a SUIT OF BLACK CLOTHES sent out for a newly accepted missionary, the death of George IV and the French revolution of July 1830 as fresh news, and a request that his son fact-check a baboon story in a magazine. AND THE LINE THAT COUNTS MOST: “KIND LOVE FROM YOUR SISTERS & BROTHER” — SISTERS PLURAL, BROTHER SINGULAR. Of the eight sons, two were alive in August 1830. 20 SEPTEMBER, READ AGAIN FROM THE FILE INSTEAD OF FROM A MAIL PREVIEW, AND IT CARRIES MORE. DR PHILIP IS NOT JUST THE COURIER — “Dr Philip was exceedingly glad to hear of you being accepted by the L.M.S. as you may well imagine, HE HAS PROMISED TO WRITE TO YOU A LETTER BY THE FIRST OPPORTUNITY”. HE SENDS A BOX: a suit of black clothes for George, and a jacket and waistcoat FOR JOHN with a further jacket, “tell him his old father has sent it him, & to make haste to fill them out”. A YEAR OF NEWSPAPERS, one number lost by Henry. AND THE HOUSE HAS FRIENDS WITH NAMES, the first in this archive who simply knew them: MR & MRS STANHOPE, MR AND MRS WARNER, and MRS FIELD AND HER DAUGHTERS — “the eldest, Miss Mary, that was, HAS MARRIED A MR BELLEW, A SURGEON”. TWO OF HIS FOUR PAGES GO ON A STORY FROM THE MIRROR about a Scottish colonist near the Xhosa whose wife was carried off by orang-outangs and recovered after two years as their queen — AND HE DOES NOT BELIEVE A WORD OF IT: “here we look upon the Story as a fictious & romance… I should be glad to hear from you, WHETHER THAT REPORT MAY BE FOUNDED IN TRUTH, OR FALSEHOOD.” A tailor of seventy, reading a cheap weekly, writing to the one man he knew who was actually there to ask whether it was true. 21 SEPTEMBER 2026 — AND THE STORY IS FOUND, AND HE WAS RIGHT. It is “A SINGULAR LETTER FROM SOUTHERN AFRICA, COMMUNICATED BY MR. HOGG, THE ETTRICK SHEPHERD”, The Mirror of Literature, Amusement, and Instruction, VOLUME XIV (1829), pages 313–318 — FICTION BY JAMES HOGG, author of The Private Memoirs and Confessions of a Justified Sinner, printed as though it were a settler’s letter home. Every detail he recalled is in it: the chief KAROO offering oxen and “a choice virgin to boot” for the settler’s wife, “he foretold I should repent it”, CAPTAIN JOHNSTONE, the wife “carried across the river by a band of pongos, (ourang-outangs)”, and her discovery as their QUEEN. AND THE DETAIL HE GOT WRONG IS WHY FIVE SEARCHES FOR IT FAILED: he thought the colonist was called “either Williams, or Williamson”, and the narrator is anonymous — IT IS HIS SON WHO IS CALLED WILLIAM. HIS FIRST WIFE MARY DIED 2 AUGUST 1814 AGED 46 and his SECOND, ALSO MARY, DIED 15 AUGUST 1824 AGED 36, both buried in the German Lutheran Church register, TNA RG 4/4631 — which is why one Mary could never be made to fit a run of baptisms from 1792 to 1819. AND THE LONDON GAZETTE HOLDS FIVE NOTICES, NOT THE ONE THIS ARCHIVE HAD. 12 MAY 1824 — the partnership of JOHN GOTLOB KOLBE AND JOHN HENRY KOLBE, of CHURCH-STREET, SOHO, TAILORS, dissolved. 30 SEPTEMBER 1836 — Kolbe and DAVID FLETCHER of Conduit-Street dissolved. 21 MARCH 1845 — “JOHN GOTLIEB KOLBE AND RICHARD DAVIES, OF CONDUIT-STREET, BOND-STREET, TAILORS, HAS BEEN DISSOLVED BY MUTUAL CONSENT”, EIGHT MONTHS BEFORE HE DIED and still calling himself a tailor, which is what the obituary’s “Esq. of Brunswick-square” has to be set against. 1824 WAS THE YEAR IT ALL WENT: the partnership dissolved in May, his second wife dead in August, and his son in the insolvent debtors’ lists in October and November. 16 SEPTEMBER, LATER — AND THE 1799 TAILORS’ LIST HAS A TWIN. In APRIL AND MAY 1834 the London press printed the roll of “considerably more than THREE HUNDRED of the Master Tailors of the metropolis” who met at Willis’s Rooms, St James’s-street, to resist THE GRAND NATIONAL CONSOLIDATED TRADES’ UNION, and the entry reads “KOLBE AND FLETCHER, CONDUIT-STREET” — Morning Post 30 April, Globe 30 April and 10 May, Old England 4 May, Morning Herald 10 May, London Courier 10 May, True Sun 10 May, Public Ledger 12 May. SEVEN NEWSPAPERS, ONE LINE. 20 SEPTEMBER 2026 — AND A HISTORIAN CALLED HIM AN APOTHECARY. The DSAB draft entry on his son opens “die seun van J.G.Kolbe, ’n DUITSE APTEKER wat in Londen woonagtig was”. THE GERMAN IS RIGHT AND THE LONDON IS RIGHT AND THE TRADE IS HIS SON’S — George Augustus sailed in 1820 as an apothecary, and the apothecary has been handed back up to the father. IT IS THE ONLY THING IN THAT ENTRY THIS ARCHIVE CAN SHOW TO BE WRONG, and it can only show it because it read the rate books. IT CLOSES THE GAP: the rate books had him in Soho to 1831 and the Gazette at Conduit Street by 1836; HE WAS AT CONDUIT STREET, WITH FLETCHER, BY 29 APRIL 1834. AND IT RHYMES WITH THE FIRST LIST THIRTY-FIVE YEARS EARLIER — in December 1799 one of 234 masters over the Combination Acts, a young man at 18 Broad-street; in April 1834 a firm with a partner and a Bond Street address, seventy years old, on the masters’ side of the same argument.

EVERT Ewert Philippus Booyzen The same name, spelt as the family said it ✝ BABA Nobody A TWELFTH CHILD. Cut with a birth star and a cross and no name at all — baba is simply baby . Not on the 1940 estate because the child was already dead when it was written.

hits.title: What changed
hits.text: → The Burgersdorp sweep of images 605–818 found five new people Taken back did A search run over part of the ground and written up as though it covered all of it. found Three. Johanna Catharina Mountjoy, born 28 January 1860, was already held in full — a daughter of George Mountjoy who married William Henry Keys — and the sweep only confirmed her and gave her a reference. Frederick Fortunatus Werdmuller was already held from a 1907 petition and a 1953 estate; what the sweep added was his birth and his mother, which is a real gain and not a new person.

hits.text: how A mistake in the archive's own working — a bug, a bad build, or a word used loosely. Where it lives now → 13 Sep 2026 was “The ancestor chart, every wife one generation too high” now The chart put each man's wife in his mother's box. Kathleen Barry stood as Willem Hermanus Booyzen's mother when she was his wife; Johanna Catharina Mountjoy stood as Petrus Jacobus Booysen's mother when she was his; and the woman at the root had no mother drawn at all. Four slots, all shifted by one. Rebuilt, and the genuinely empty slot — the mother of the 1812 man — is now a wall. how A mistake in the archive's own working — a bug, a bad build, or a word used loosely.

hits.title: Disputed
hits.text: A different John Barry. → Willem Hermanus Booyzen (1851–1905) Death at Indwe annotated “To be confirmed, not sure” — and his son David Schalk is born in 1907. Resolved RESOLVED by the 1905 death registration: he died at Doorn Street, Indwe on 13 September 1905 of a stomach ulcer. The date is right; David Schalk cannot be his son. → Johanna Catharina Mountjoy (1819–1863) Dies 19 May 1863 (probate-sourced) — but Izak (1864) and Stephanus Francois (1875) are recorded as her sons. She also carries three conflicting birth facts. Serious Petrus Jacobus remarried and the second wife is missing from the tree. Two “sons” belong to her. → Anna Maria van der Merwe (1785–1825) Dies before 8 March 1825 — but Hendrik Stefanus is recorded born 23 August 1829.

hits.title: Method
hits.text: Seventeen people had a page that said “This person is recorded in the archive’s index but is not yet discussed on any page.” Among them the 1820 Settler , whose name the built site carries 155 times ; John Barry , 158; George Mountjoy , 140; Petrus Jacobus Booysen , 110; Johanna Catharina Mountjoy , 89. What went wrong The gatherer that collects every mention of a person dropped any name that was a strict prefix of a longer person’s name . The rule was written for a good reason — to stop John Barry collecting every mention of John Barry Booyzen — and it was implemented as “delete the shorter man” rather than “let the longer name go first”.

johanna-catharina-mountjoy-of-indwe.r: She joined the Dutch Reformed congregation at Indwe on 23 JULY 1907, arriving FROM BARKLY OOST — six weeks after Willem Hermanus Booijzen was confirmed in the same church — and the register’s last column records her dead there in June 1911. A Mountjoy and a Booyzen in one small colliery congregation, twenty-two years after the two families stood at the same font at Barkly Oost. 15 SEPTEMBER 2026 — AND THERE IS NOW A CANDIDATE BIRTH DATE, NOT ENTERED. The baptism transcriptions indexed by gendatabase.com hold a JOHANNA CATHARINA MOUNTJOY BORN 28 JANUARY 1860, one of four Mountjoy children baptised between 1858 and 1864. She would be FIFTY-ONE in June 1911. IT IS NOT BEING TAKEN: this family already contains a Johanna Catharina Mountjoy born 1819, so the name repeats within it, and WHAT WOULD DECIDE IT IS THE CONGREGATION THE 1860 BAPTISM WAS REGISTERED IN — which is the field that site charges for. If it is Barkly East or its district, the two women are almost certainly one. 17 SEPTEMBER 2026 — AND SHE HAS A JOINING DATE. The Indwe LIDMATE register enters her on 23 JULY 1907 — FamilySearch 1:1:6PR3-HNWZ — SEVEN WEEKS AFTER WILLEM HERMANUS BOOIJZEN WAS CONFIRMED IN THE SAME CONGREGATION on 31 May 1907. This archive had her death at Indwe and nothing before it. It does not make the two families relatives; it makes them neighbours, in one small coal town’s register, in one winter.

A Johanna Catharina Mountjoy born 28 January 1860 would be fifty-one in June 1911. It is a candidate and it is not being entered.

hits.text: The query re-surfaced him; it did not find him. He remains exactly what he was: an unresolved second William, indexed twice over to Graaff-Reinet and Dordrecht , eight years after the Burgersdorp baptism . On Henry Jaonas there is an argument, and it comes entirely out of figures this archive already held. John Augustus Barry II was born 13 March 1847 and baptised four weeks later — a documented date, off a register. James Henry Barry is carried in this archive as born "about 1847" , and that figure is not a register at all: it is an age worked back from his death at Barkly East on 23 June 1939. Two brothers cannot both be born in 1847 , and the approximate date is the one that has to give way.

hits.title: What changed
hits.text: Two other entries independently confirmed de Villiers on two of Jan Booijsen's sons, which strengthens the book against the death notice. And the relationship search on the father, queued as Question 13, returned a household: John Augustus Barry II had a wife and nine children this archive had never seen, including the Kolbe name carried into a fourth generation. The book was read, and it contradicted the death notice Found found A G2G answer named de Villiers 1893 as downloadable, so it was downloaded and read rather than taken on trust — which is the whole point of this archive, and it cut against yesterday's conclusion.

hits.title: What was taken back
hits.text: how A document read wrongly, or a conclusion drawn past what the document says. Where it lives now → 13 Sep 2026 was “The 1915 notice named eight children and the archive listed nine” now Two men on that list — John Augustus Barry II and George Augustus Barry — had no page at all, while a ninth name stood in their place. All three fixed together; the build now refuses to publish a household naming somebody who does not exist. how A mistake in the archive's own working — a bug, a bad build, or a word used loosely.

john-barry.r: One profile holding two men — and on 14 September 2026 they came apart. THE YORKSHIRE MAN IS NOW A LIFE: born at WHITBY in 1796; resident at BILSDALE MIDCABLE when he took a licence on 2 October 1838 to marry MARGARET JACKSON of Beadlam at Helmsley; and in the 1851 census a SHIP OWNER at SHIP YARDS, RUSWARP, WHITBY, aged 55, married, head of his household — the ONLY John Barry of that age in the whole Yorkshire census. John Barry deaths are then registered in the WHITBY district in 1858 and in 1860. He outlived the Cape man, who died at de Bruins Poort in 1853, by at least five years. THEY ARE TWO MEN. What this archive still does not have is the Cape one: no birth, no arrival, no burial. And a caution worth keeping — a Whitby SHIP OWNER is exactly the kind of man whose son could be born AT SEA, which is what John Augustus Barry's death notice says of 1819. That coincidence is not evidence, and the censuses say it is not the same man.

hits.text: What went wrong The gatherer that collects every mention of a person dropped any name that was a strict prefix of a longer person’s name . The rule was written for a good reason — to stop John Barry collecting every mention of John Barry Booyzen — and it was implemented as “delete the shorter man” rather than “let the longer name go first”. So the moment anybody added George Augustus Kolbe of Wakkerstroom , George Augustus Kolbe stopped existing as far as the build was concerned. Why it is worth a section The data was never wrong. Every record, every document, every citation was intact and on disk the whole time.

john-gerson-eliezar-kolbe.v: “Jan” · JOHN GERSON ELIEZER KOLBE, in his obituary · Commandant Kolbe
john-gerson-eliezar-kolbe.r: THE SETTLER'S ELDEST CHILD, AND UNTIL TODAY A LINE IN A TABLE. His obituary — Grahamstown Journal, 15 April 1868, headed “DEATH OF COMMANDANT KOLBE” — gives the whole man. Born 7 JULY 1822; married 3 APRIL 1843 to ANNA JACOBA VAN DER MERWE; DIED 3 APRIL 1868, ON HIS WEDDING ANNIVERSARY, at the farm LEEUWBERG, of TYPHUS OR TYPHOID CAUGHT ON COMMANDO — “thus adding another to the long list of victims of our miserable war”. He had settled on KAALSPRUIT about 1850 and lies there — AND HE CONFIRMS THE FARM HIMSELF. A lost-property advertisement he placed in the Friend on 9 MARCH 1864 is signed “J.G.E. KOLBE, Kafferberg, Kaalspruit” (the address as the paper printed it). The Friend’s own obituary transcription reads “[Randspruit]”, bracketed by the transcriber as doubtful; the man’s own address settles it. THAT ADVERTISEMENT ALSO PUTS THE TWO BROTHERS IN ONE DOCUMENT: it concerns “a promissory note, date 9th March 1864, drawn by GEORGE AUGUSTUS KOLBE in favor of J.G.E. KOLBE, payable 4 months after date for £154 Stg” — lost on the Market Square at Bloemfontein. HE LEFT A WIDOW AND TWELVE CHILDREN — “OF THE EIGHT SONS AND FOUR DAUGHTERS HE HAS LEFT BEHIND HIM”, which is the Friend of the Free State’s own wording and a count the Grahamstown reprint drops. Only one daughter was married and the youngest child was an infant; TWO SONS HAD BEEN SERVING WITH HIM IN THE FIELD and “proved themselves amongst the bravest of our burghers”. NONE OF THE TWELVE IS NAMED AND NONE IS IN THIS ARCHIVE. 20 SEPTEMBER 2026 — A COLLABORATIVE TREE NAMES THEM, AND IT IS NOT THIS FAMILY’S OWN. A Geni profile for FREDERIK FORTUNATUS KOLBE, born 22 October 1857 at Bloemfontein and dead there 18 December 1930, gives him as SON OF COMMANDANT.GEN. JOHN GHERSON ELIEZER KOLBE AND ANNA JACOBA, and lists as his siblings CATHARINA WILHELMINA MAGDALENA PIENAAR ANDERSON, GEORGE AUGUSTUS, GENERAL WILLEM JOHANNES, JAN HENDRIK and PETRUS JACOBUS “and 6 others” — which is twelve. THIS IS FROM A USER TREE, NOT FROM A DOCUMENT, and none of the twelve is adopted here on it — it is a lead and not a witness. But TWO OF ITS CLAIMS MATCH DOCUMENTS THIS ARCHIVE REACHED INDEPENDENTLY: his wife MARIA PETRONELLA ELIZABETH ANTOINETTE and daughter ROSA MAGDALENE against the 1890 Bloemfontein baptism already held, and his daughter MARIA MARGARETHA DOWNING ROUSSEAU against TAB MHG 5450/68, an orphan index entry here that now has a father. VAB MHG M777 IS STILL THE DOCUMENT THAT WOULD PROVE THEM, and it is a better thing to order now that there is something to check it against. He was COMMANDANT OF THE DISTRICT, A JUSTICE OF THE PEACE, A DIRECTOR OF THE BLOEMFONTEIN BANK and a DEACON of the Dutch Reformed Church, and he had spoken in the VOLKSRAAD in May 1867. He had refused public life for twelve years after THE ABANDONMENT, having protested the British withdrawal and applied to SIR GEORGE CLERK for compensation for his land so that he might leave with the troops; failing that, “he, like many more, had to cast his lot with the Free State”. AND ON HIS DEATHBED, in full possession of his senses, he told the doctor and the others present THAT THIS STATE HAD TAKEN TOO MUCH LAND FROM THE BASUTOS, that he had always thought so and had said so in the Raad, and begged them to rescind the resolution and treat with the Governor for an equitable boundary. 20 SEPTEMBER 2026 — A HISTORIAN’S DRAFT NAMES HIM TOO, AND NAMES THE WAR. The DSAB entry on his father says the eldest son “J.G.E. KOLBE (1822–68), was later op LEEUBERG naby Bloemfontein woonagtig en het gedurende die TWEEDE SOTHO-VRYSTAATOORLOG roem verwerf as KOMMANDANT”. BOTH YEARS MATCH THIS ARCHIVE TO THE YEAR — born 7 July 1822, dead 3 April 1868 — and both were got from an obituary and an auction advertisement that the entry does not cite. It is the strongest of the nine places where that entry and this archive agree from different documents. AND IT NAMES WHAT KILLED HIM: the obituary said only “our miserable war”; the war was the SECOND SOTHO–FREE STATE WAR. AND HE MAY BE IN THE 1830 LETTER, AGED EIGHT. Read from the file rather than from a mail preview, MSB 751 encloses “a Jacket & waistcoat FOR JOHN & a further Jacket also for him, tell him HIS OLD FATHER has sent it him, & TO MAKE HASTE TO FILL THEM OUT”. CLOTHES FOR A GROWING CHILD, sent from Soho to the Cape in August 1830, when this man was eight years old and the eldest son of the house. IF IT IS HIM IT IS THE EARLIEST DOCUMENT IN THIS ARCHIVE THAT MENTIONS HIM. “His old father” is the difficulty and is not glossed over — the writer is his GRANDFATHER, and this is an inference, not a reading.

john-henry-kolbe.d: 13 Apr 1832, buried 22 Apr 1832, German Lutheran Church
john-henry-kolbe.r: ONE OF THE EIGHT SONS, AND THE ONE WHO LIVED LONGEST OF THOSE FOUND. Baptised 29 July 1800, father John, mother Mary, batch I02559-1. TNA RG 4/4631 folio 100: died 13 April 1832, buried 22 April, AGED 32 — twelve years before the obituary that counted him among the seven already gone. AND HE SPEAKS. Old Bailey, session of 13 January 1819, trial t18190113-149 — Richard Kerr indicted for stealing “one coat, value 6l., the property of JOHN HENRY KOLBE”. His own deposition: “MY FATHER IS A TAILOR, AND LIVES IN CHURCH-STREET, SOHO. On the 9th of January, about eleven o’clock at night, I stopped at the Star and Crown public-house, Westminster, and left my coat over my horse’s head — I had a chaise standing at the door; I saw the prisoner go out, and suspected him — I went out, and missed my coat.” NOT GUILTY. HE WAS EIGHTEEN, and his brother George Augustus sailed for Algoa Bay the following year. It is the only voice this archive has from the Soho house, and it corroborates the rate books’ address from a source that had no interest in it. AND THE LONDON GAZETTE SAYS WHAT BECAME OF HIM. 12 MAY 1824, issue 18027 page 796: the partnership of “JOHN GOTLOB KOLBE AND JOHN HENRY KOLBE, OF CHURCH-STREET, SOHO, IN THE COUNTY OF MIDDLESEX, TAILORS” dissolved — father and son, in business together, at the address he gave the court five years earlier. Then 9 OCTOBER and 16 NOVEMBER 1824, issues 18069 page 1668 and 18080 page 1900, in the INSOLVENT DEBTORS lists, petitions to be heard at Portugal-Street, Lincoln’s-Inn Fields on 5 November: “KOLBE, JOHN HENRY (SUED AS HENRY KOLBE), FORMERLY OF NO. 22, NORFOLK-STREET, MIDDLESEX-HOSPITAL, AND LATE OF NO. 4, MANSFIELD-PLACE”. HE WAS TWENTY-FOUR, OUT OF THE FAMILY BUSINESS AND OUT OF SOHO IN THE SAME YEAR HIS STEPMOTHER DIED, and he was dead at thirty-two. 20 SEPTEMBER 2026 — AND HIS FATHER WRITES ABOUT HIS DYING. MSB 751, the letter of 23 August 1830 to his brother at the Cape: “HENRY had wrote to you himself & left his letter at the Mission house to be forwarded to you… he keeps up pretty well at present, but what effect the winter may have upon him if it should set in very cold, as it did last winter, is perhaps not doubtful, since it must prevent him from taking exercise by walking, & which is a great means of keeping down THE DROPSY, OF WHICH HE BEARS STILL THE SYMPTOMS… I trust also that you will join your prayers, that he may vouchsafe to prepare him to a fit state of meeting his God… HE APPEARS AT PRESENT TO BE RESIGNED TO THE CATASTROPHE.” HE HAD TWENTY MONTHS LEFT. And the same letter’s closing — “kind love from your SISTERS & BROTHER” — makes him THE LAST OF THE EIGHT SONS ALIVE BESIDES GEORGE AUGUSTUS, so that the obituary’s “last remaining of eight sons” became true on 13 April 1832, twelve years before it was printed. AND HE MARRIED THREE MONTHS AFTER THE TRIAL: Westminster Marriages — JOHN HENRY KOLBE AND MATILDA FORD, 26 APRIL 1819, ST MARGARET WESTMINSTER, both of that parish. He was eighteen. A MARY ANN MARIA FORD KOLBE MARRIED AT WHITECHAPEL IN THE FIRST QUARTER OF 1847 — GRO index volume AZ, 840, page 16 — and “Ford” carried as a forename is how families carried a mother’s maiden name. SHE IS VERY PROBABLY HIS DAUGHTER. AND THE PRESS GIVES HIS TRADE, WHICH THE GAZETTE DID NOT. Law Chronicle, Commercial and Bankruptcy Register, 13 January 1825: “KOLBE John Henry, of Norfolk-street, Middlesex-hospital, LAST OF MANSFIELD-ST., KENTISH TOWN, TAILOR, DRAPER” — so he set up on his own account in his father’s trade, and the Gazette’s “Mansfield-Place” is Mansfield Street, Kentish Town. THE MAY 1824 DISSOLUTION WAS REPORTED IN AT LEAST SIX LONDON PAPERS, all of them putting HIS name first: “J. H. Kolbe and J. G. Kolbe, Church-street, Soho, tailors”. AND THE 1830 LETTER SHOWS HIM DOING AN ORDINARY THING. Packing a year of newspapers for the Cape, his father notes one number missing — “the one of the 4th of Decr last, which cannot be found, supposing that HENRY, WHO HAS THEM EVERY WEEK, AFTER I HAVE DONE WITH THEM, — has lost”. The father read the paper first and the son had it after. IT IS THE ONLY DESCRIPTION THIS ARCHIVE HAS OF WHAT ANYBODY IN THAT HOUSE DID WITH AN ORDINARY EVENING, and he had four months to live when it was written.

hits.title: The documents
hits.text: This is John Henry Kolbe , baptised at Westminster on 29 July 1800. This archive has his font, his deposition in the Old Bailey in January 1819 ( “my father is a tailor, and lives in Church-street, Soho” ), his marriage to Matilda Ford three months later, his bankruptcy in 1824, and his burial in the German Lutheran register on 22 April 1832. Now it has his illness, and his father’s grief, twenty months before the end.

SIX MONTHS AFTER HIS FATHER DIED HE IS HOLDING STOCK IN HIS OWN RIGHT BESIDE HIS MOTHER. In 1884 The Friend reported that the eldest son of “Mr. John KOLBE”, a boy of ten called LITTLE JANNIE, was struck dead by lightning on his father's farm five hours north of Bloemfontein; the Natal Witness index carries the same death and names the father GEORGE. Two papers, two fathers, and this archive will not choose.

Sawtelle of Cambridge, England, was announced in the Eastern Province Herald on 16 October 1944, in the last winter of the war. magdalena-booijsen-of-1782.r: b3c4d6 — SISTER of Petrus Jacobus, the man at the head of this archive's documented line, and six years older. De Villiers's volume 1 records her marriage only as “gehuwd met H. A. VILJOEN”; volume 3 gives it in full from the Viljoen side — HERCULES ALBERTUS VILJOEN, baptised 30 March 1777, burgher at Graaff-Reinet, MARRIED 26 FEBRUARY 1797. Seven children, of whom the seventh is ADRIANA CHRISTINA, BAPTISED 19 AUGUST 1810 — the name and the age of the woman her nephew David Schalk married at Cradock in 1828. IF THAT IS THE SAME WOMAN, THIS AUNT IS ALSO A MOTHER-IN-LAW.

Her 1920 Sterfkennis — estate 44420, stamped Pretoria 16 August 1920 — names her parents as Jan Gerhardus Lodewicus Booyzen and Magdalena Susanna Maria, gives her age as 59 years 9 months, and lists seven children. Her son-in-law B. J. van den Berg signed it.

hits.title: What changed
hits.text: Lichtenburg joins the line Found found The same correction does the opposite favour. Vaalbank, in the district of Lichtenburg, is where the 1876 man's son died in 1885 — and this archive had already read a 1920 Sterfkennis from that farm for Magdalena Susanna Maria van den Berg, born Booyzen about 1860, father entered as Jan Gerhardus Lodewicus Booyzen, filed under “NOT PROVED”. She is his daughter. Two deaths on one farm thirty-five years apart, which is settlement rather than passage. Read west along the atlas: Rustenburg 1876, Lichtenburg 1885 and 1920, Marico 1903.

hits.title: The documents
hits.text: The direct ancestor died in district Rustenburg in 1876 — twenty-five years before the war, a generation before Johannesburg. Two other notices read the same afternoon sit in the same country: a Magdalena Susanna Maria van den Berg, born Booyzen , who died at Vaalbank in the district of Lichtenburg in 1920 and whose father is entered as Jan Gerhardus Lodewicus Booyzen ; and an an Anna Johanna Booijzen , born in the district of Cradock about 1823, who died on a farm in the district of Rustenburg in 1891, leaving children called Petrus Jacobus, Magdalena Johanna and Hendrik Stephanus Nicolaas.

margaret-downing.d: 2_ Nov 1867, Burgersdorp — the day illegible on the stone
margaret-downing.r: THE ANSWER WAS ON A PHOTOGRAPH THIS ARCHIVE HAS HAD ALL ALONG. The Burgersdorp monument is on the Kolbe page, and the caption quoted it as far as “ALSO HIS RELICT MARGARET DOWNING…” AND STOPPED THERE. The stone goes on: “BORN IN LONDON 23 FEBRUARY 1803 AND DIED AT BURGHERSDORP 2_ NOVEMBER 1867.” HER BIRTH IS NOW A DATE — 23 February 1803, where this archive had “c. 1804” — AND THE DEATH IS SETTLED AT 1867. Her son’s obituary of 15 April 1868 said she had died “about three months since”, which would have been January 1868; it was nearly five months, and a journalist rounding is a journalist rounding. THE DAY IS A 2 AND A DIGIT THAT WILL NOT RESOLVE at any magnification, and is not guessed. The Cape estate ran on: MOOC 13/1/253 no. 2, “DOWNING, MARGARET, WIDOW OF KOLBE, GEORGE AUGUSTUS. LIQUIDATION AND DISTRIBUTION ACCOUNT”, 1869 — and she had made a WILL OF HER OWN in 1854, MOOC 7/1/295 no. 70, ten years after she was widowed. Married at fifteen in Shoreditch, signing with a mark. Died owning a house and a farm. 20 SEPTEMBER 2026 — HER MOTHER IS STILL NOBODY, AND THAT IS NOW A TESTED POSITION RATHER THAN A GAP. A user tree gave her as MARY KING POOLEY (1768–1834); this archive’s own copy of the tree gives MARY P KING. FindMyPast holds exactly ONE Downing–Pooley marriage before civil registration — JOHN DOWNING and MARY POOLEY at WELCOMBE, DEVON, 10 MAY 1802, nine months and thirteen days before Margaret’s birth — AND THAT COUPLE STAYED IN DEVON, baptising a child at Welcombe in 1803 and more in 1806, 1809 and 1810, where Margaret was born in LONDON. RULED OUT. And the last Downing record in that parish is A MARY DOWNING BURIED THERE IN 1834, which is the year both trees give her mother’s death — SO “POOLEY” IS VERY PROBABLY A PREVIOUS RESEARCHER’S RECONSTRUCTION out of one Devon marriage and one Devon burial, and not a record at all. FROM A USER TREE, NOT ADOPTED. Her own 1867 death notice asks for her parents and answers “Both dead”, naming neither. AND THERE IS A CERTIFICATE, IN A MUSEUM. The DSAB draft on her husband lists among its sources “ALBANY MUSEUM, GRAHAMSTAD: FOTOKOPIE VAN DIE HUWELIKSSERTIFIKAAT VAN G.A. KOLBE (1819)”. THIS ARCHIVE HOLDS THE ALLEGATION AND NOT THE MARRIAGE — the sworn statement made to get the licence, which is where the false age was sworn, and not the register entry that followed it. A photocopy of the certificate has been sitting in Grahamstown since before 1992. The same entry gives her dates as “(1803–1867)”, WHICH IS WHAT THE BURGERSDORP STONE SAYS, from a source that had not read the stone this way.

His grandfather was George Augustus Kolbe — who married at sixteen on a sworn lie in Shoreditch, sailed on the Nautilus in 1819 as an 1820 Settler , preached across the Orange River, and named a Karoo farm after the Württemberg his own father had left. His grandmother was Margaret Downing of London. Both of them lie under a cut-stone monument at Burgersdorp — names, London birthplaces, farm and dates carved into it — about forty miles from where that notice was written. The family forgot them inside seventy years, with the headstone still standing. And it had happened before, on the other side of the house.

hits.text: The children's list is further down the page and had never been read. It names EIGHT: John Augustus, James Henry, GEORGE AUGUSTUS (new), Henry Nicholas, Frederick Fortunatus, Richard Peter, Margaret Mary Bedford and KATHLEEN MARY BOYSON, born Barry, married in community of property to William Boyson — the only Booyzen marriage on the list, spelled Boyson by an English clerk. margaretha-wilhelmina-elizabeth-mary-kol.r: His wife, married 1846. Daughter of the 1820 Settler — and the reason the Kolbe name runs through the Booyzens. Her own DEATH NOTICE 1291, filed by her son R. P. Barry at Barkly East in May 1915, THREE YEARS after she died, gives her age as 84, her nationality as AFRIKANDER OF EUROPEAN EXTRACTION, her father as “Kolbe, thinks James was Christian name” and her mother as UNKNOWN. She died in R. P. Barry’s house at Manorowen and left NOTHING — no movable property, no immovable, estate Nil, no will. And she names NINE children where her husband’s notice names eight. The ninth is WILLIAM.

hits.title: The cousin marriage
hits.text: George was Kathleen's son. Anna was Hendrik's granddaughter. They were first cousins once removed , and their common ancestors are John Augustus Barry I and Margaretha Wilhelmina Elizabeth Mary Kolbe . What follows from it Catherine Mary Sophia Booyzen descends from John Augustus Barry I and Margaretha Kolbe twice — once through her father, once through her mother. This is pedigree collapse : she has fewer distinct ancestors than the arithmetic of generations predicts.

hits.title: The documents
hits.text: Checked one by one against the register here, nearly all of them were already held: Harriet Louisa Barry , dead at Manor Owen on 7 September 1912; Henry James Kolbe Barry , whose 23 June 1939 is already on his record; John Gerson Eliazer Barry ; James Jonathan Mountjoy , dead at Barkly East on 22 December 1937; and Margaretha Wilhelmina Elizabeth Mary Kolbe , dead at Manorowen on 2 August 1912. That is worth saying rather than quietly not saying. A sweep that returns almost nothing new is a measurement of how thoroughly the ground was already worked, and this ground was worked properly. The work-list row assumed otherwise. One discrepancy, recorded and not adopted.

hits.title: The cousin marriage
hits.text: The Schoemans sit alongside the Barrys in the same way. P. Schoeman witnessed the 1879 Booysen–Barry marriage ; Anna Johanna Maria Schoemann married Hendrik Nicholaas Barry in 1877; and the 1901 Pretorius–Barry wedding was held at the home of D. Schoeman . Why that matters → The names give it away Anna's mother was christened Margarietha Wilhelmina Elizabeth Barry — the same four names, in the same order, as her own grandmother Margaretha Wilhelmina Elizabeth Mary Kolbe . And Anna herself was "named after Anna Johanna Maria Schoemann" , her father's mother, a fact the tree records explicitly rather than leaving to be inferred.

margrith-louisa-maria-barry.v: Margreth Louisa Mary — and the index gives her no surname at all
margrith-louisa-maria-barry.r: ONE OF THE TWO MISSING BARRY CHILDREN, FOUND 16 SEPTEMBER 2026 — and open question 13 has been asking for her since this site was written. The 1903 registration of her father's death says ELEVEN children; his own death notice names eight and her mother's names nine. SHE IS IN THE BURGERSDORP REGISTER AND NOT IN ANY NAME SEARCH, BECAUSE THE INDEX GIVES HER NO SURNAME: two separate index passes of the same page read “MARGRITH LOUISA MARIA” and “MARGRETH LOUISA MARY”, and the Name column stops there. It is the blank Name column again, the same failure that hid her sister Catherine Mary Sophia of 1855. Found by asking the index for a RELATIONSHIP — father John Barry, mother a Kolbe — and letting it return whatever the child was called. Her parents are entered as “Margrith Willemina Kolbe + John Barry”. SHE IS ALMOST CERTAINLY THE “MARGARET MARY” NAMED ON HER PARENTS' DEATH NOTICES AND NEVER PLACED: it is her mother's name, and there is no other candidate in the sibling group. ark:/61903/1:1:6VYG-SS94 and 1:1:6F4L-76PK.

hits.title: The documents
hits.text: So of the three figures the archive had, the marriage register is the outlier : it gives his age as 22 in December 1879, when he was 28 . His 1905 death registration says 55 , which is right within a year. The 1879 entry is wrong by six years. And he was named for his godfather The witnesses are Willem Hermanus Pieterzen , Maria Catharina Magdalena Potgieter and Xaverius Hermanus Pieterzen . (The archive scan corrects this archive's earlier reading of the surname as Pietersen — see below; the first given name, earlier read as Iwerus , is still not certain.) Johanna Catharina Mountjoy's half-brothers were Pieterzens — the sons of Anna Catharina Sleer by her first marriage. The archive had them only as names in a list.

maria-johanna-kolbe.v: Maria Johanna Kolbe van der Merwe
maria-johanna-kolbe.r: HER STONE IS READ AND IT NAMES HER CHILDREN THE WAY THIS FAMILY ALWAYS DOES. “IN LIEFDEVOLLE HERINNERING AAN ONS MAMMIE — MARIA JOHANNA VAN DER MERWE (GEB. KOLBE) — 26 OKT. 1886 – 1 OKT. 1953 — Wat hy doen is wel gedaan.” And underneath, six household names: MARTZI · P.S. · JUDIE · PIETMAN · CHARL EN SUZAN. THE BIRTH IS NOW A DATE — 26 October 1886, where this archive had only the year — and THE SIX CHILDREN ARE NEW. This is the THIRD stone in this archive to list children by what they were called rather than what they were registered as: the Booyzens at Silverton, the Kolbes at Wakkerstroom, and now this. BORN AT WAKKERSTROOM AND DEAD AT WAKKERSTROOM, sixty-seven years apart, in a town her grandfather had never seen. Her 1953 estate file is the document that names the whole household: FATHER George Augustus Kolbe, MOTHER Martha Sophia Klopper, HUSBAND Charl Daniel van der Merwe. Her birthplace is entered as “Wakkerstroomn, Transvaal, Blanke Unie-burger” — the clerk's spelling, and the Union's category.

hits.title: Open Questions
hits.text: Here are three named Mountjoys in the right district, twenty-six years after her death. Answered They are the descendants of Johanna Catharina Mountjoy's brother. George Mountjoy (b. 1823, Cradock), saddle maker , married Maria Sophia Botha at Cradock in 1848 and had thirteen children. Hercules Johannes (the father at the 1889 font) and James/Jakobus Jonathan (the witness, who died at Barkly East in 1937) are two of his sons. The child baptised that day, George Mountjoy (1889–1963) , was a second cousin of the Booyzen daughter baptised in the same register three weeks earlier.

hits.text: Whether it was DELIVERED is a separate question from whether it was sent, and this archive will not use the second word until it has checked for the first. A dead child's name, given again — watched happening Found found Worked out of the register rather than off a new document. Hercules Johannes Mountjoy and Maria Sophia van Niekerk baptised a daughter at Dordrecht on 6 September 1896 and called her CAROLINA ISABELLA MARGARETHA ALETTA, her grandmother's four names entire. She died at Wodehouse on 25 October 1897, aged fourteen months. On 8 November 1901 they had another daughter and gave her the whole name again; she married Hendrik Stefanus Palm, and a granddaughter born in 1920 carries it still.

martha-angeline-kolbe.r: HER STONE IS READ, AND IT TAKES BACK WHAT THIS ARCHIVE SAID THIS MORNING. “TER GEDACHTENIS VAN ONS GELIEFDE KLEINE — MARTHA ANGELINE KOLBE — GEBOREN 9 OCT. 1901 — OVERLEDEN 8 DEC. 1901 — HEBR. 6”, and cut across the base, the mason’s town: NEWCASTLE. IT STANDS IN WAKKERSTROOM MAIN CEMETERY, NOT AT VOLKSRUST. The index this archive read gives her burial as “Volksrust, Eastvaal District Council” — which is the DISTRICT, not the town, and Wakkerstroom lies inside it. WITH THE TOWN GOES THE CAMP: a family stone in a town churchyard, in Dutch, cut by a monumental mason twenty-five miles away in Natal, is not a camp burial, and this archive should not have gone near the word. She was sixty days old, she died in the middle of the war, and that is all that can be said. She carries the name of her great-aunt Martha Angelina, baptised at Colesberg in 1868.

martha-sophia-klopper.r: HER HALF OF THE STONE: “MOEDER — MARTHA SOPHIA (GEB. KLOPPER) — GEB. 27 MEI 1867 — OORL. 14 OKT. 1950 — Ons dank God elke maal as ons aan haar dink.” The birth is new; the death matches the civil register to the day. Married George Augustus Kolbe of Wakkerstroom AT SEVENTEEN, about 1885 — the fourth bride in this archive married before eighteen, and the third in the Kolbe line. Named as the mother on her daughter Maria Johanna's 1953 estate file, which is how this archive learnt she existed. She died four years before her husband.

hits.title: The Kolbes
hits.text: He is baptised at Colesberg on 11 October 1863 — and he dies at Wakkerstroom , in the eastern Transvaal, on 28 September 1954, aged ninety-one . The age counts exactly from the font. In between he married Martha Sophia Klopper , who was seventeen; their eldest was born at Wakkerstroom in 1886; and he was dead at ninety-one before this archive existed. A prisoner of war, and this archive nearly gave him to the wrong man. WO 108/368 , the master list of Boer prisoners numbers 1–32561, holds a George Augustus Kolbe, aged 40, nationality Transvaaler, residence Wakkerstroom, prison Natal, 1902 .

mary-elizabeth-kolbe.v: Maria Elizabeth Kolbe, in her estate notice · Enslin
mary-elizabeth-kolbe.r: HER DEATH IS NOW DATED, AND SHE DIED WITHOUT A WILL. The Friend of the Free State, 23 October 1863, twice in two weeks: “Derwyl MARIA ELIZABETH KOLBE zonder testament na te laten is overleden en de nagebleven echtgenoot G.F. ENSLIN by brieve van administratie ter vereffening van haren boedel als executeur is aangesteld” — she had died INTESTATE and her husband was appointed executor of her estate. This archive had only “before 1867”, inferred. It is now BEFORE 23 OCTOBER 1863, from a notice her own husband placed. MARGARETHA'S SISTER, and the woman who married GEORGE FREDERICK ENSLIN — which is the whole answer to a contradiction this archive carried as Serious, that Margaretha appeared to marry Enslin while married to John Barry. It was resolved from Margaret Downing's 1867 death notice. The Burgersdorp register of 23 October 1853 shows it instead: the two sisters baptising a son each, two entries apart, on one page.

hits.text: It was resolved from Margaret Downing’s 1867 death notice , which lists among her children “Mary Elizabeth (dead) who was married to George F. Enslin” . The Enslin marriage belongs to Margaretha’s sister . Here are the two sisters, on one page, on one day, baptising a son each. Mary Elizabeth Kolbe with her Enslin, Margareth Kolbe with her Barry, two entries apart in the Burgersdorp register on 23 October 1853. The contradiction → And it puts them at Burgersdorp. The 1915 death notice says the marriage was at “Burghersdorp (probably)” — a son guessing, sixty-five years on, at something nobody had told him.

hits.title: The Booyzen Archive
hits.text: There is no photograph of their farm, and this archive does not invent one. This archive was built for David Defranceski , born in Johannesburg, living in Brisbane. It runs backwards from his grandmother Catherine Mary Sophia Booyzen (1929–2013) — who married Nuno Fernando Lerena at St Joseph's, Mayfair, in 1949 — into the north-eastern Cape: to Barkly East and Dordrecht , to Cradock and Graaff-Reinet , and out again to Württemberg , to Soho , and to a County Cork that may or may not be real. It is a public archive with one rule: the living are left out — omitted, not hidden. And a second rule, which is harder: every claim says how well it is known.

ockert-johannes-stephanus-booysen.r: Signed his father’s 1908 death notice as “son of the deceased” — thirty-two years after his father had signed his own father’s at Brakfontein. Second of the seven children on his mother’s 1891 notice, and he carries HER father’s name: Ocken Johannes Oliefier. hits.title: What changed
hits.text: Her father was Jacob Dormehl; her mother is entered UNKNOWN, by a husband of ten years, which makes seven death notices in this archive that fail to name a parent. She had one wagon and her furniture, worth £51 8s 0d, and she left a will. Looking for Ockert's estate and finding his son's Found found Ockert Johannes Stephanus Booysen died at Klerksdorp on 16 January 1921 and HAS NO ESTATE FILE OF HIS OWN in the indexed Transvaal probate records. Searched under Ockert, Okkert, Ocker and Ocken against Booysen, Booyzen and Booijsen: six hits, every one of them him as somebody else's relative — four duplicate copies of a 1935 Sterfkennis where he is the father, and two of his own father's 1908 notice where he is entered Child.

hits.title: The documents
hits.text: There is no b , no r-t-s , and no second syllable that could carry -berts . Oliefier is how a man who writes Booijzen , Stefanes and Brakfontijn spells OLIVIER. And the archive does not have to guess, because her own son wrote her name down again . Seventeen years later, filling in his father's death notice, Ockert Johannes Stephanus Booysen gave the first wife as "Anna Catharina Johanna Booysen, born Olivier" . The 1908 notice → Three documents, three spellings of one woman: Anna Johanna on her own notice, Anna Catrena on her son's, Anna Catharina Johanna on her husband's. Put together, she is Anna Catharina Johanna Olivier , and every one of them agrees on the surname. Seven children, all of age Question twelve, entire.

hits.text: Still marked Serious. This archive is not going to decide a father on a city. THE OTHER MOVED FURTHER THAN EXPECTED. Ockert Johannes Stephanus Olivier and Anna Catharina Botha MARRIED AT GRAAFF-REINET ON 8 DECEMBER 1816 — index only, no image — and have four children baptised at Cradock between 1820 and 1826: Gert Cornelis, Aletta Catharina, Anna Johanna and an Ockert Johannes Stephanus the younger. GRAAFF-REINET is the Booysens' own town.

petrus-jacobus-booyzen.r: HIS STONE IS READ AND IT CONFIRMS BOTH DATES EXACTLY: “HIER RUS — MY GELIEFDE SEUN — PIETER J. BOOYZEN — GEB. 29 DES. 1904 — OORL. 7 JUNIE 1937 — NA DIE KRUIS DIE KROON.” Dead at thirty-two. AND ONE WORD OF IT DOES REAL WORK: “MY geliefde seun”, not “ONS”. A stone cut by ONE surviving parent — and his mother Isabella Frederika had been dead seven years when he died, so the parent is his father, GERT JACOBUS, who then lay down beside them both fourteen years later. Three of one household in one cemetery, and the grammar of the inscriptions gives the order they went in. Baptised in the Dutch Reformed register with a Z, son of Gert Jacobus Booyzen and Isabella Frederika Coetzee — the second marriage's line, at Middelburg, spelled Booyzen a year before the Indwe sheet.
